# Testing

This doc covers how to check changes in this project: the headless compile check, the hand-rolled static test suites under `Assets/Scripts/Tests`, the Play-mode scenario harness, and in-game manual testing. It replaces `Assets/Scripts/Tests/README.md`, `Assets/Scripts/Tests/AidAnother_ManualTestScenarios.md` and `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Combat/SleepSpell_ManualTestScenarios.md`.

The suite results dated 2026-10-07 (section 3.2) and the scenario-harness runs of 2026-10-07 (sections 3.4 and 3.5) come from Play-mode and edit-mode runs through the Unity MCP; other claims about runtime behavior come from reading the code. Known test problems are tracked with stable IDs in [issues/TST.md](issues/TST.md) (index: [KNOWN_ISSUES.md](KNOWN_ISSUES.md)); IDs from other areas point to the matching `issues/<PREFIX>.md` file.

## 1. Testing levels at a glance

| Level | How to run | What it catches | What it misses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compile check | `bash tools/compile_check.sh` (about 5-7 s, no Editor needed) | C# compile errors in all of Assembly-CSharp, test code included | Runtime behavior, scene/asset problems, Editor-folder code, player-build-only errors |
| Static suites | The committed runner `Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner`: menu **Tools > DND Tests**, or `RunFromCommand` through the Unity MCP (section 3); an edit pass, then a Play pass | Rule regressions in mechanics that have a suite, compared against the known-failures baseline `tools/tests/static-suites.json` | Anything without a suite (section 2.2); suites that pass on a bug |
| Scenario harness | `Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioHarness.Start` through the Unity MCP in a fresh Play session (section 3.4), or `ScenarioHarness.QueueFresh` from edit mode for one fresh Play session per filter (section 3.5) | Whole fights in the real game loop with seeded and forced dice: invariant violations, combat ends the game misses, soft locks, per-scenario rule expectations, same-seed determinism; the AI-vs-AI soak against DMG random encounters (section 3.5) adds per-side action counts as an AI-depth baseline | The PC path for AI-run party members (they take the NPC turn path); prompts other than the AoO confirmation, the counter-trip prompt, the full attack's 5-foot step prompts (always skipped), the grapple natural-attack menu, the Haste chooser, the Improved Grab menu, the Cleave target menu, the escape-opposition and overrun avoid-or-block prompts (answered by the runner) and the "Overrun or Normal Move" dialog (answered by the `OverrunTo` step); anything no scenario or invariant looks at |
| Manual testing | Play `Assets/Scenes/MainScene.unity`, use presets and the F12 panel (section 4) | UI flow, targeting, AI, end-to-end combat | Anything you do not look at |

### Compile check

`tools/compile_check.sh` reuses the compiler response file Unity last generated (`Library/Bee/artifacts/*/Assembly-CSharp.rsp`), keeps its defines and references, replaces the source list with the current `Assets/**/*.cs`, and runs Unity's bundled Roslyn (`F:/Unity/<version>/Editor`, override with `UNITY_DIR`). The DLL goes to a temp dir; `Library/` is not touched. `VERBOSE=1` prints every warning.

- Requires that Unity has opened the project once on this machine (so the `.rsp` exists). If packages or scripting defines change, the `.rsp` is stale until Unity regenerates it.
- Compiles with the Editor defines (`UNITY_EDITOR`, `ENABLE_LEGACY_INPUT_MANAGER`, LangVersion 9.0), so it cannot detect code that only breaks a player build (for example `using UnityEditor` outside `#if UNITY_EDITOR`).
- Skips every path containing `/Editor/` (there are none today), analyzers and source generators. It does not import assets or create `.meta` files.
- Baseline at 0dd8e76: `exit=0 errors=0 warnings=508` (507 since batch 11 step 7, 2026-10-15, removed the unused `blockedByGlobe` local of the old `PerformSpellCast`, a CS0219), of which 479 are CS0618 (obsolete API: mostly the string overloads of `ItemDatabase.CloneItem`/`ItemDatabase.Get`, then `FindObjectOfType`). Treat any error, or a jump in the warning count, as a regression.

Run it after every code change. All test files compile into the game assembly, so a broken test breaks the game build too.

## 2. Static test suites

### 2.1 How a suite is written

There is no test framework: no `com.unity.test-framework` in `Packages/manifest.json`, no `.asmdef`, no `[Test]` attributes. A suite is a plain class:

- `public static class <Name>Tests` in namespace `Tests.<Folder>` (`Tests.AI`, `.Character`, `.Classes`, `.Combat`, `.Feats`, `.Inventory`, `.Magic`, `.Maneuvers`, `.Mounts`, `.Services`, `.Utilities`). Exceptions in the global namespace: `CraftingSystemTests`, `Phase5IntegrationTests`, `RodTests`.
- Entry point `public static void RunAll()` (97 suites). It resets private static `_passed`/`_failed`, logs a header such as `====== SLEEP SPELL RULES TESTS ======`, calls the database `Init()` methods (all idempotent), runs `private static void TestXxx()` methods, and logs a summary such as `====== ... Results: N passed, M failed ======` (the format varies; the runner reads the counters directly, section 3). It returns nothing.
- Most suites have their own private `Assert(bool condition, string testName, string detail = "")` that logs `  PASS: <name>` with `Debug.Log` or `  FAIL: <name> <detail>` with `Debug.LogError` (example: `Tests/Combat/SleepSpellRulesTests.cs:37-49`). Variants (`AssertEqual`, `AssertTrue`, ...) follow the same pattern. Exception: `Phase5IntegrationTests` logs `FAIL:` with plain `Debug.Log`, so its failures do not show under the Console Error filter.
- 19 suites also expose a snake_case alias such as `class_level_feature_progression_test() => RunAll()` (`Tests/Character/ClassLevelFeatureProgressionTests.cs:15`). Nothing calls them.
- Tests build characters with `new GameObject()` + `AddComponent<CharacterController>()` + `CharacterController.Init(stats, pos, null, null)` + `InventoryComponent.Init(stats)`, clean up with `Object.DestroyImmediate` in `finally`, and reach private members through `System.Reflection` (19 test files, about 60 `GetMethod`/`GetField`/`GetProperty` reflection calls; TST-006).

### 2.3 Runners that exist

- **`Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner`** (`Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runner/StaticSuiteRunner.cs`, all inside `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, not in an `Editor/` folder so the compile check covers it) discovers and runs every suite. Section 3 describes it.
- `Tests.Services.ServiceTestRunner.RunAll()` runs 9 suites in sequence: SpellUtilities, SpellCastingHelper, TeamUtility, ConcentrationService, DispelMagicService, CombatLogHelper, SpellTargetingService, CombatCalculationService, DiceService. The committed runner supersedes it and does not discover it (its name does not end in `Tests`). It has no exception isolation and a stale header comment (TST-024). Nothing calls it.
- Three suites are MonoBehaviours whose `Start()` calls `public static void RunAllTests()`: `Tests.Combat.FlankingReachRulesTests`, `RangeCalculatorTests`, `ReachWeaponRulesTests`. They are attached to nothing; the runner calls `RunAllTests()` directly and reads their `N passed, M failed` summary line, because they have no `_passed`/`_failed` fields.
- No production code calls any `RunAll`. `Encounters/DungeonEncounterTableExamples.RunAll()` is an example dump, not a test; the runner skips it by name.

### 2.4 Shared helpers

| Helper | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Tests.Utilities.TestHelpers` | Used by 7 suites (AIProfileFramework, CharacterTagSystem, CreatureImmunityRules, AttackCalculator, EconomyService, SavingThrowResolver, BlinkCastRules) | `EnsureCoreDatabasesInitialized` (Race, Class, Item, Feat, Spell), `CreateStats`, `CreateCharacter` (named args, optional `gridPosition`), `CreateWarrior/Rogue/Cleric`, `ResetActions`, `Cleanup`. HP is `level*4 + CON mod`, not real hit dice. |
| `TestHelpers.SetGridPosition` / `GetDistance` | Avoid | `SetGridPosition` sets `GridPosition` correctly but places the transform at `(x*5, 0, y*5)`; `GetDistance` measures world distance between transforms. The game uses `SquareGridUtils.GridToWorld` = `(x, y, 0)` and `SquareGridUtils.GetDistance` (3.5e diagonals). Set `GridPosition` and use `SquareGridUtils.GetDistance` instead. |
| `Tests.Utilities.MockCharacterFactory` | Unused | Commoner/Fighter/Skeleton/Goblin. `CreateSkeleton` has no undead type. |
| `Tests.Utilities.TestFixtures` (`D35TestBase`, `CombatTestBase`) | Unused | `D35TestBase` adds a GameManager (see pitfalls). |

The other 90 suites define their own local `BuildStats`/`CreateController`/cleanup helpers.

### 2.6 Pitfalls

IDs refer to [issues/TST.md](issues/TST.md) unless another prefix is given.

- **GameManager singleton.** 14 suites call `new GameObject().AddComponent<GameManager>()`. `GameManager.Awake` (`_Core/GameManager.cs:483-490`) schedules `Destroy` on the new object and returns early if `GameManager.Instance` already exists (in MainScene, SceneBootstrap creates one), so the test instance has no services; tests patch `_conditionService` in by reflection. In a scene without a GameManager the test instance becomes `Instance`, runs the full Awake, and `Instance` is left pointing at a destroyed object after cleanup (nothing resets it). `DispelMagicRulesTests.cs:244-273` takes a different branch depending on which case applies. Results can depend on the scene (TST-007, TST-005).
- **SquareGrid.Instance is overwritten.** `SquareGrid.Awake` sets `Instance = this` unconditionally (`Grid/SquareGrid.cs:25-28`). Six suites add their own SquareGrid, so after a run `SquareGrid.Instance` points at a destroyed grid. Code that falls back to it (`CharacterController.CurrentGrid`, `CharacterController.cs:11974`, `GameManager.cs:5183, 5387, 5473`) is affected. The runner puts `SquareGrid.Instance` back after each suite; a suite called by hand does not. Restart Play mode after running suites before playtesting (GRID-010, [issues/GRID.md](issues/GRID.md)).
- **Static state.** Databases, `ItemDatabase` registrations and `UnityEngine.Random` state are static and persist for the whole Play session (Enter Play Mode Options are off, so a new Play session resets them). Suites that call `Random.InitState(seed)` never restore the previous state, and `DiceService.Roll` uses `UnityEngine.Random` directly with no seeding API (TST-010); a test can instead force single dice through `ScenarioHooks.RollFilter` (section 3.3) and must clear it in `finally`. The runner seeds each suite and restores `Random.state` after the pass, restores `GameManager.Instance` and `SquareGrid.Instance` when a suite replaced them, and destroys root GameObjects a suite left behind. It does not reset static databases, registrations or other static fields, so suites can still affect each other and the game in the same Play session.
- **GameSettings auto-creates a GameObject.** `GameSettings.Instance` (`_Core/GameSettings.cs:22-38`) creates a `GameSettings` object if none exists. `CharacterStats.ApplyPendingLevelUp` reads it to pick the HP mode (default Roll, random), so level-up HP in tests such as `MulticlassSkillRulesTests` is random. Left Ctrl+H (`Utilities/DebugCommands.cs`, self-bootstrapped via `RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod`) cycles Roll/Average/Maximum in Play mode.
- **Rings, rods and wondrous items are not in ItemDatabase after `ItemDatabase.Init()` alone.** `SceneBootstrap.cs:1036-1063` calls `RingDatabase.Init`, `WondrousItemDatabase.Init`, `RodDatabase.Init` and then `RegisterAllRingsInItemDatabase` / `RegisterAllInItemDatabase`. A test that looks those items up through `ItemDatabase.Get` must do the same.
- **Play mode is required** for some suites: `AreaEffectManager.Instance` calls `DontDestroyOnLoad` (`Spell/AreaEffects/AreaEffectManager.cs:13-21`), which only works in Play mode; `ConcealmentRulesTests` uses it directly (indirect use from other suites not checked). `CharacterController.Init` uses the `SpriteRenderer` that `Awake` creates, and `Awake` does not run on `AddComponent` in edit mode, so every suite that calls `Init` throws `NullReferenceException` in edit mode (TST-009).
- **Assigning `controller.Stats` instead of calling `Init`.** In Play mode `Awake` has already added a `ConditionManager` with no stats, so conditions applied to such an actor are dropped without a word; in edit mode the `CharacterStats` fallback path runs instead of `ConditionManager` (TST-029). An actor whose `GridPosition` is never set stands in the same square as every other such actor, and `CharacterController.Attack` refuses the attack as out of range. Build actors with `TestHelpers.CreateCharacter` (or `Init`) at explicit adjacent positions.
- **Exceptions inside a suite.** Only 3 test files contain a `catch`, so one exception skips the rest of that suite and its summary line. The runner catches it, records the exception type, message and three stack frames, still reads the suite's counters, and goes on with the next suite.
- **Reflection breaks at runtime, not compile time.** Renaming private members such as `GameManager._conditionService`, `_activeSummons`, or `CharacterController.EstablishGrappleWith` breaks tests silently. About 18 test files make about 48 `GetMethod`/`GetField`/`GetProperty` calls. Grep `Assets/Scripts/Tests` for the member name before renaming (TST-006).
- **Namespace shadowing.** Inside any `Tests.*` namespace, `Inventory` resolves to the namespace `Tests.Inventory`; write `global::Inventory` for the class (TST-011).
- **CharacterStats constructor order** is `..., str, dex, con, wis, intelligence, cha, ...` (WIS before INT, `Character/Stats/CharacterStats.cs:3345`). Use named arguments.
- **Static Play passes after scenario-harness fights.** A static Play pass run in the same Play session as harness fights once reported false `GrappleDamageRulesTests` regressions (34 unexpected "NPC melee sequence" / "AI stopgap" failures) that a fresh session did not show; the cause is unknown (TST-035). The runner adds a warning when the harness started fights earlier in the session (`ScenarioRunner.JobsStartedThisDomain`). Run static Play passes in a fresh Play session after harness runs.
- **Tests ship in player builds.** No asmdef or `#if` guard; the three MonoBehaviour suites appear in the Add Component menu (TST-013).

### 2.7 Writing a new suite

1. Create `Assets/Scripts/Tests/<Folder>/<Name>Tests.cs` with `namespace Tests.<Folder>` and `public static class <Name>Tests`.
2. Copy the `RunAll`/`Assert` skeleton from `Tests/Combat/SleepSpellRulesTests.cs:12-49`: reset counters, header log, database init (that file calls `RaceDatabase`/`ClassRegistry`/`ItemDatabase`/`SpellDatabase.Init()` directly; `TestHelpers.EnsureCoreDatabasesInitialized()` also covers `FeatDefinitions`), test calls, summary log.
3. Build characters with `TestHelpers.CreateCharacter(...)` using named arguments; set `GridPosition` directly.
4. Wrap each test body in `try/finally` and destroy everything you created, including any GameManager or SquareGrid.
5. Prefer public API. If reflection is unavoidable, `Assert` that the `MethodInfo`/`FieldInfo` is not null instead of silently returning a default.
6. Do not add `Assert(true, ...)` placeholders. If something cannot be tested yet, log a warning that does not count as a pass.
7. If you seed `UnityEngine.Random`, save `Random.state` first and restore it in `finally`.
8. Run the compile check, then run the suite with the runner (`RunFromCommand("filter=<Name>Tests")`, section 3) and paste its line from `static-<mode>.txt` into your change notes. Add an entry for the suite to `tools/tests/static-suites.json` (`needs`, and any known failures with their issue IDs), or the runner reports it as NEW.

## 3. Running suites

`Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner` (`Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runner/StaticSuiteRunner.cs`) is the committed runner. The whole file is inside `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, so it does not ship in player builds; it is not in an `Editor/` folder, so `compile_check.sh` compiles it.

**Entry points.**

- Menu **Tools > DND Tests > Run Static Suites (current mode)**, **List Static Suites** and **Write Proposed Baseline**. Each logs its summary to the Console.
- From a Unity MCP `CommandScript`: `Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner.RunFromCommand("<options>")` returns a summary of at most about 4,000 characters (verdict, totals, the non-passing suites, file paths). `ListSuites()` lists every discovered suite with its `needs` and reports NEW and MISSING suites. `Run(StaticRunOptions)` returns the full `StaticRunReport`. The types are public because the MCP's script assembly cannot see internal members.
- `StaticSuiteRunner.RanInPlayModeThisDomain` is true once a Play pass ran in this domain (it resets when Play mode is entered again).

**Discovery.** Every non-nested type in Assembly-CSharp whose name ends in `Tests` and declares a parameterless `public static void RunAll()` (preferred) or `RunAllTests()`, sorted by full name. That gives 157 suites today (2026-10-29, after batch 13 step 7 added `Tests.AI.KnowledgeFactsTests`; 156 after batch 13 step 6 added `Tests.Combat.ActionPanelParityTests`; 155 after batch 13 step 4 added `Tests.Combat.TotalDefenseRulesTests`; 154 after batch 13 step 3 added `Tests.Combat.ActionCatalogTests`; 153 after batch 12 step 24 added `Tests.Character.ArmorSpeedTests`; 152 after batch 12 step 22 added `Tests.Grid.MovementLegalityTests`; 151 after batch 12 step 17 added `Tests.Combat.AttackSequenceStepTests`; 150 after batch 12 step 13 added `Tests.Combat.PostAttackQuirkSetsTests`; 149 after batch 12 step 12 added `Tests.Combat.AttackLegalityTests`; 148 after batch 12 step 10 added `Tests.Character.SaveRollRulesTests`; 147 before it; 146 after batch 12 step 4 added `Tests.Character.NpcSkillFallbackTests`; 145 after batch 12 step 3 added `Tests.Combat.ActionLimitRulesTests`; 144 on 2026-10-16; batch 11 step 29 replaced `Tests.Services.SpellResolutionServiceTests` with `Tests.Magic.BlinkCastRulesTests`; 144 after batch 11 step 28 added `Tests.AI.AiMetamagicPlannerTests`; 143 after batch 11 step 25 added `Tests.AI.AreaAimSearchTests`; 142 after batch 11 step 24 added `Tests.Magic.AreaOriginTests`; 141 after batch 11 step 23 added `Tests.Magic.AreaRoutingTests`; 140 after batch 11 step 20 added `Tests.Magic.AreaDamageOneRollTests`; 139 after batch 11 step 19 added `Tests.Magic.CustomSpellDiceTests` and `Tests.Magic.MetamagicOnSpellTests`; 135 on 2026-10-15 (132 `RunAll`, 3 `RunAllTests`), after batch 11 step 14 added `Tests.Magic.CasterLevelRulesTests`; 134 after batch 11 step 7 added `Tests.Magic.CastCoreStageOrderTests`; 133 after batch 11 step 5 added `Tests.Magic.SpellHandlerRegistryTests`). `ServiceTestRunner` and `DungeonEncounterTableExamples` do not end in `Tests` and are not run.

**Mode gating.** Each suite's `needs` comes from the baseline (`play`, `edit`, `either`, `unknown`; a suite missing from the baseline counts as `unknown`).

- A Play pass runs `play`, `either` and `unknown` suites. It records whether a scene `GameManager` existed (`sceneGameManager`) and warns when it did not.
- An edit pass runs only `edit` suites: CauseFear and Scare, which fail in Play mode because of TST-007, and the 10 suites that build actors without `Init` and lose their conditions in Play mode (TST-029). In edit mode those 10 run the `CharacterStats` condition fallback, not `ConditionManager` (section 2.5), so they do not cover the game's condition path until TST-029 moves them back to `play`. It runs inside a temporary additive scene that becomes the active scene, then restores the previous active scene and closes the temporary one without saving. It never saves a scene.
- `all=true` ignores the gate and baseline skips; suites run in the wrong mode are marked `modeMismatch`.

**Refusals** (verdict `REFUSED`, nothing runs, only `static-<mode>.txt` is written, so the JSON of an interrupted pass stays resumable): Unity is compiling; scripts have compile errors; Unity is entering or leaving Play mode; `STALE_CODE`; a resume that does not match (see `after=`); or, in an edit pass, the temporary scene cannot be created (for example while an untitled scene is open). `STALE_CODE` means the loaded code may not be what is on disk: a `.cs` file under `Assets` is newer than both `Library/ScriptAssemblies/Assembly-CSharp.dll` and the last edit-mode script import, or the dll was rebuilt after the domain loaded. Whether Unity recompiles an edit made during Play mode depends on the per-user preference *Script Changes While Playing*, so the runner checks instead of assuming. A file whose timestamp changed without a content change (for example after `touch`) is not reimported by `AssetDatabase.Refresh()` and keeps tripping the check; once a refresh compiled nothing, pass `allowStaleCode=true`.

**Isolation, per suite.**

- Suite logs are captured by swapping `Debug.unityLogger.logHandler` (plus `Application.logMessageReceived` for engine messages) and are not echoed to the Console unless `echo=true`, so Console Error Pause does not stop a run. With `echo=true` the suites' FAIL `LogError` lines reach the Console, and Error Pause can leave Play mode paused after the call; the summary then shows `paused=true`, and `ExitPlaymode` still works.
- Exceptions are caught; the result records the type, message and three stack frames, and the run goes on.
- When the seed is not 0, `UnityEngine.Random` is seeded with `seed XOR FNV-1a(full name)` before the suite. The state from before the pass is restored at the end.
- New root GameObjects in the loaded scenes (and, in Play mode, the DontDestroyOnLoad scene) are counted in `leakedCount`, named in `leaked` (first 10) and destroyed (`cleanupLeaks=false` keeps them).
- Known game leaks (`KnownLeakIssues`, by root name) are destroyed too but reported as one aggregated `knownLeaks` entry per name, for example `Name x12 (ISSUE-ID, destroyed)`. The list is empty since UI-001 was fixed on 2026-10-08: before, every combat log call orphaned 50 `PooledLogMsg` lines at the scene root (588 in one FlankingReach run). A stray `PooledLogMsg` root now counts as an ordinary leak.
- Lazily created singletons that keep a static `Instance` are kept and listed under `singletonsCreated` (with `xN` when more than one): `AreaEffectManager`, `WindEffectManager`, `ExperienceCalculator`, `GameSettings`, `DebugCommands`.
- `GameManager.Instance` and `SquareGrid.Instance` are put back if the suite replaced them (TST-007, GRID-010); the result lists them under `restored`.
- Files that appear in the project root during a suite are listed under `strayFiles`. Only names on the runner's allowlist (`phase5_6_test_results.txt`, the old Phase5 dump) are deleted; any other file is marked `(kept)`, because it may not belong to the suite.
- The runner does not reset static databases, registrations or other static fields.

**Counts.** The runner reads the suite's private static `_passed`/`_failed` fields (also after a throw). Without them it uses the last `N passed, M failed` line, else it counts PASS/FAIL marker lines. `noSummary` flags a suite with counters but no summary line that did not throw.

**Failure labels.** Each captured line that matches `[Tag] FAIL:`, `[FAIL]`, `❌` or `✗` becomes a label: the tag and markers are stripped and duplicates merged, at most 60 kept. `failureCounts` (parallel to `failures`) records how many FAIL lines carried each label, so an assertion text used twice (RapidShot's "Rogue should have Rapid Shot feat") counts twice. Other error logs and exceptions are counted as `errorLogCount` with 5 samples; they are informational only.

**Options** (space-separated `key=value` tokens):

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `filter=A,B` | Run only suites whose full name contains one of the entries (case-insensitive) |
| `all=true` | Ignore the mode gate and baseline skips |
| `seed=N` | Seed base; the default is the baseline's `seed` (20261007). `seed=0` does not seed the suites, so they continue from the session's `Random.state`; the runner restores that state after every pass, so repeated `seed=0` passes in one Play or editor session start from the same state and repeat each other. For a spread, sweep explicit seeds (`seed=1`, `seed=2`, ...), as the 2026-10-07 sweeps did |
| `echo=true` | Also send suite logs to the Console; FAIL lines then trigger Console Error Pause, which can leave Play mode paused (`ExitPlaymode` still works) |
| `cleanupLeaks=false` | Keep leaked root objects |
| `maxSeconds=S` | Stop starting new suites after S seconds; the report has `complete=false` and `resumeAfter`, and the TXT and summary print the full resume options |
| `after=<FullName>` | Resume: run only suites sorted after this one and merge into the existing report of the same mode. Refused unless that report is incomplete, `after` equals its `resumeAfter` or `currentSuite`, and `filter`, `seed` and `all` match; copy the printed `resume with ...` options. The report records `resumedFrom` |
| `writeBaseline=true` | Also write `Logs/TestRunner/static-baseline-proposed.json` |
| `allowStaleCode=true` | Run despite a `STALE_CODE` refusal |

**Result files** in `Logs/TestRunner/` (git-ignored by `/[Ll]ogs/`):

- `static-<play|edit>.json`: the full report (`JsonUtility`). It is written when the pass starts, before each suite (with `currentSuite` set to it) and after each suite, with `complete=false` and `resumeAfter` = the last suite with a result until the pass ends. If Unity froze or crashed, `currentSuite` names the suite that hung. Fields: runId, startedUtc, unityMode, sceneGameManager, seedBase, filter, all, after, resumedFrom, maxSeconds, codeLoadedUtc, durationMs, complete, verdict, resumeAfter, currentSuite, totals, newSuites, missingSuites, warnings, and per suite: status (`pass`, `fail`, `error`, `skipped`), skipReason, modeMismatch, countSource, passed, failed, noSummary, seed, durationMs, exception, failures, failureCounts, errorLogCount and samples, leaked, leakedCount, knownLeaks, singletonsCreated, restored, strayFiles and the baseline diff.
- `static-<mode>.txt`: overwritten with a `RUNNING` header when the pass starts, so an old result is never mistaken for the current one. At the end: a header with run id, mode, seed, scene GameManager, totals and verdict; one line per suite run, for example `FAIL  Tests.Combat.RapidShotTests  48/54  known 0  new 6  0.0s`; then the sections REGRESSIONS, STALE, NEW/MISSING, LEAKS and WARNINGS. Read this first.
- `static-<mode>.log`: every captured line, with a `### <suite>` separator per suite, written at the end (a `RUNNING` line until then). After a resumed run it holds only the suites of the last call.
- The summary's last line lists the files this call wrote; a refusal writes only the TXT.

**Baseline** (`tools/tests/static-suites.json`, versioned, outside `Assets` so it has no `.meta`): `{ "version": 1, "seed": 20261007, "suites": [ ... ] }` with one entry per suite: `type` (full name), `needs`, `skip` (non-empty text skips the suite unless `all=true`), `expectThrow` (an exception type name, for example `TargetParameterCountException` for CharmPerson, TST-001), `passed`, `failed`, `flakyFailures`, `knownFailures` (a list of `{ "match", "issue" }`, where `match` is an ordinal prefix of a failure label and `issue` an issue ID) and `notes`. The runner never writes this file; `writeBaseline=true` writes a proposal to curate by hand: new failure labels get the issue `TODO`, and an exception seen in the run becomes `expectThrow` with `TODO: issue ID for <Exception>` appended to `notes`. The loader warns about known failures with an empty or `TODO` issue, and about an `expectThrow` whose `notes` have no issue ID (or a `TODO`).

**Verdicts.**

- A suite is a REGRESSION when it throws without a matching `expectThrow`, or when its failures not explained by a known label exceed `flakyFailures`. Unexplained = the larger of (unmatched labels + labels beyond the cap) and (the suite's failure count minus the FAIL lines whose label matched, capped at the failure count). Failures without a FAIL line therefore count as unexplained; suites that print each failure twice (Crafting, Rod, Phase5) are not penalized.
- A suite with no baseline entry (NEW) that fails or throws counts as a REGRESSION too and is listed under REGRESSIONS with `(no baseline entry)`.
- It is STALE when a known failure was not seen, or when `expectThrow` is set and it did not throw.
- A drop in total assertions against the baseline counts is a warning.
- The pass verdict is REGRESSION, else STALE, else OK. It is `NO_BASELINE` when the file is missing (a malformed file is reported and the run continues without a comparison) and `REFUSED` when the pass could not start (see Refusals). NEW (discovered, no entry) and MISSING (entry, not discovered) suites are listed; a NEW suite changes the verdict only when it fails or throws.

A label that matches only some seeds is left out of `knownFailures`, so that a run with another seed does not report it as STALE. When you fix a known failure, delete its entry (the runner reports it as STALE until you do) and update `passed`/`failed`. When you curate from `static-baseline-proposed.json`, change only the entries your fix touched: the proposal lists every unmatched label of that run as a `TODO` known failure, including the seed-dependent MagicCircle and SunderInventoryRemoval labels, which would then go STALE with other seeds; copy such a label only if a seed sweep shows it fails with every seed. TouchOfIdiocy reseeds the RNG itself, so its two known failures depend on the order of `Random` calls and can go STALE after an unrelated change (TST-031).

### 3.1 Running suites through the Unity MCP

When the Unity MCP is attached to this project (check that `Application.dataPath` and the console paths it reports are under `F:/DNDPrototype`):

1. In edit mode, after script changes, call `AssetDatabase.Refresh();` and check `!EditorApplication.isCompiling` and `!EditorUtility.scriptCompilationFailed` in the next call.
2. Edit pass: `result.Log(Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner.RunFromCommand(""));`.
3. `EditorApplication.EnterPlaymode();` as the only statement of its call. Entering Play mode reloads the domain; the next MCP call runs once Play mode has started, but it can fail with a named-pipe error when the reload is slow (see the notes below and TST-037). Character creation is enough, because suites build their own characters.
4. Play pass: `result.Log(Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner.RunFromCommand(""));`. A full Play pass of the 87 Play-mode suites takes about 3 s (2.8 to 3.2 s on 2026-10-07) and the edit pass about 0.2 s, so `maxSeconds` is a safety net; if you set it, resume with the printed `resume with ...` options until `complete` is true.
5. Read `Logs/TestRunner/static-play.txt` (and the JSON for detail) with the Read tool. Check that the `runId` and `started` time in its header are newer than the call that started the pass: the files keep the last pass that finished, which may be an older one.
6. `EditorApplication.ExitPlaymode();`. Suites leave static state behind, so do not play by hand, and never run the scenario harness, in a Play session that ran suites.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEditor;

internal class CommandScript : IRunCommand
{
    public void Execute(ExecutionResult result)
    {
        if (!EditorApplication.isPlaying) { result.LogError("Enter Play mode first."); return; }
        result.Log(Tests.Runner.StaticSuiteRunner.RunFromCommand("filter=BullRushRulesTests,RapidShotTests"));
    }
}
```

Notes:

- A filtered suite whose `needs` does not match the current mode is skipped (it shows in the `skipped` count only): run `edit` suites (CauseFear, Scare and the 10 TST-029 suites) in edit mode, or pass `all=true`.
- For a seed sweep, call `Run(new StaticRunOptions { Filter = "...", Seed = n })` in a loop in one `CommandScript` and collect `suites[i].failures`; 67 seeds of one suite take a few seconds.
- The MCP refuses some namespaces in a `CommandScript` (for example `System.Reflection`); call the runner's public API instead.
- `Unity_GetConsoleLogs` output is too large to read whole; the runner's files are the record.
- Enter Play Mode Options are off (full domain reload). Exit Play mode before editing scripts. Whether Unity recompiles an edit made during Play mode depends on the per-user preference *Script Changes While Playing*; on 2026-10-07 it did not, and the old code kept running. The runner refuses with `STALE_CODE` in that case.
- If Unity freezes in a suite (an endless loop, a stack overflow), the owner has to kill and restart it. Then read `currentSuite` in `Logs/TestRunner/static-play.json`, add a `skip` for that suite to the baseline with the reason, and resume with the options for `after=<currentSuite>` (same filter and seed); the runner warns that the suite has no result.
- `AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset` fails through the MCP ("User interactions are not supported").
- The MCP connection can drop across a domain reload, whether it comes from entering Play mode or from a refresh that recompiles scripts: the call then fails with "Named pipe socket file not found", though later calls work. On 2026-10-09 this happened four times: twice on Play-mode entry (the CHR-019 run and the batch 8 attempt, the first call after `EnterPlaymode()`) and twice on edit-mode `AssetDatabase.Refresh()` calls (the bonus stacking session). The likely cause is TST-037: in a long editor session every domain reload grows slower (173 to 180 s by then, against about 3.5 s after a restart). Before a Play pass or a batch, read the last `Domain Reload Profiling:` figure in `C:/Users/Hoyty/AppData/Local/Unity/Editor/Editor.log` (`grep -aF` it; the file can be gigabytes); if it is more than about 30 s, restart the editor instead of starting the run: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools/restart_unity.ps1` (the owner allowed agents to run it on 2026-10-29; it closes the editor, force-stops it after 90 s, reopens the project and waits until the window shows MainScene and `Editor.log` is quiet; about 80 s; never while a scenario batch is queued, because `ScenarioBatchDriver` keeps its queue in SessionState), then check `Application.dataPath` and the active scene through the MCP. The MCP reconnected by itself after the first such restart (2026-10-29, first reload 5.6 s). After the owner's restart of 2026-10-09 the reloads were 3.1 to 3.4 s (one of 6.5 s) through the whole batch 8 regression, and no MCP call failed.

### 3.3 Scenario harness seams

The scenario harness (section 3.4; the soak and fresh-session batches are section 3.5) drives real fights in Play mode. It relies on:

- `_Core/ScenarioHooks.cs`: inert static hooks (dice filter, attack, AoO, maneuver, threatened-cast, cast begun (NPC path and, since batch 11 step 3, the PC pipelines), cast stage, move, condition, combat-log and phase events, scripted AI turns, forced initiative head, input suppression). Raise sites and what each one covers are listed in [architecture/combat-and-grid.md](architecture/combat-and-grid.md#scenario-hooks-test-instrumentation). Install handlers through `ScenarioHooks.Safe` and `ScenarioHooks.SafeTurn` and fail the run when `ScenarioHooks.HookErrors` is not empty. Call `ScenarioHooks.ClearAll()` when a run ends. Leftovers are also cleared: Enter Play Mode Options are off, so statics survive leaving Play mode, and `Tests/Scenarios/ScenarioSessionGuard.cs` (editor only, `[InitializeOnLoad]`) restores fast mode and clears the hooks on ExitingPlayMode and EnteredEditMode; `StaticSuiteRunner.Run` does the same before a pass and adds a report warning when anything was still set.
- `_Core/GameManager.ScenarioHarness.cs` (editor only, `internal`): `Harness_IsReady`, `Harness_SetupPartyFromCreation` (returns a reason when level-ups queued by creation were left unapplied), `Harness_SetupPartySlot` (set BAB through `BaseAttackBonusOverride`, CHR-068), `Harness_DeactivatePartySlot`, `Harness_SpawnEnemies` (the squares given, through the game's spawn placement; a negative square gets the default layout; the runner then places exact actors with `MoveToCell`), `Harness_StartCombat`, `Harness_HaltCombat` (stops GameManager and TurnService coroutines, so run the harness on its own MonoBehaviour), `Harness_ResetWorld` (runs every step even if one throws and returns the failed steps; summons are destroyed at the end of the frame), `Harness_RestorePartyAfterCombat`, `Harness_DumpState`, `Harness_PendingPrompt` (the open AoO confirmation, ranged retarget, full-attack 5-ft choice or special-style submenu, else null), `Harness_CancelToActionChoices`, `Harness_OpenSpecialAttackMenu` (presses Special Attack and reports whether the menu opened; a selecting flag already set before the press is reported, never cleared), `Harness_PressSpecialAttackButton` (clicks the open menu's button for a maneuver type, refused when that button is hidden or disabled), `Harness_SelectSpecialAttack`, `Harness_SelectSpell`, `Harness_SetPendingCast`, `Harness_GetPendingSpell` and `Harness_GetPendingMetamagic` (set and read the pending cast's spell and metamagic with no other effect; they replace reflection on `_pendingSpell` and `_pendingMetamagic`, TST-006, which are read-only views of the current cast's request since batch 11 step 29; with no cast open a spell opens a scratch Ui cast and null ends it), `Harness_OpenCastCount`, `Harness_CurrentCastRequest` and `Harness_EndAllCasts` (the per-cast context stack, batch 11 step 4), `Harness_CancelSelection` (right-click or Escape, `HandleInputCancelRequested`: the player backs out of a target selection or preview; `rules/spell-save-dc`'s handler Heighten check uses them), `Harness_ApplySpellBuff` (a buff spell's effect through `ApplySpellBuff`, the effect step of a landed cast, without slot or action; pass a clone), `Harness_AnswerTouchSpellPromptDischargeLater` and `Harness_ChooseFirstSelectionOption` (the Discharge Later button and the open selection list's first option, for the `CastHeld` and `CastChoosing` steps; batch 11 step 3, 2026-10-15, with the read accessor `CombatUI.Harness_FindFirstSelectionOption`), `Harness_SpawnSummonedCreature` and `Harness_DespawnSummon` (the game's summon spawn `SpawnSummonedCreature` for a caster, cell and summon option, without initiative or the active summon list, and its immediate removal from the grid, the summon trackers, initiative, `NPCs` and the AI behaviour list), `Harness_PendingAoO`, `Harness_AnswerAoO`, `Harness_PendingCounterTripDefender` and `Harness_AnswerCounterTrip` (the counter-trip prompt, CMB-079; `Harness_HaltCombat` and the combat reset drop an unanswered one). `Harness_ResetWorld` also releases every party, pool and summon grapple before the summons are destroyed: grapple links are static and outlive a halted fight (CMB-038), and without that a reused slot started the next job still grappling. Two editor-only read accessors back this: `CombatUI.Harness_IsSpecialAttackMenuOpen`, `Harness_FindSpecialAttackButton`, `Harness_OpenSpecialStyleMenuName`, `Harness_FindSpecialStyleOption` and `Harness_FindSpecialStyleCancel` (the open selection submenu, its option by label and its Cancel button; CMB-127, CMB-124), and `CharacterController.Harness_GrappleLinkHolders` (the static link table, read without ending any link). Both party setups reset a slot that held a character through `GameManager.ResetPCSlotForNewCharacter` (the same `ResetCharacterSlotForSpawn` the enemy spawns use, CRE-046) before `Init`: `Harness_SetupPartySlot` directly and `Harness_SetupPartyFromCreation` through `SetupCreatedCharacters`. So a party character of one job does not inherit the previous job's Power Attack, Fighting Defensively, Rapid Shot, readied counterspell, attack pool, AI maneuver memory, tags, trackers, mount, feint windows, turn state, spell effects or spellcasting component, and casters get a fresh `SpellcastingComponent`. The harness does not reset enemy pool slots itself: `Harness_SpawnEnemies` goes through `SetupEnemyEncounter` and `InitializeNPCFromDefinition`, which first calls `GameManager.ResetCharacterSlotForSpawn` (CRE-046, fixed 2026-10-08), so every spawned slot starts as a fresh controller: no trait, component, spell effect, grapple or mount link, tag, AI memory or profile of its earlier creature (the old profile is destroyed only when the GameManager created it, never one the harness assigned), and no other character's feint window, readied counterspell, remembered square, concentration or aura save immunity tied to it (the list is in [architecture/characters-and-creatures.md](architecture/characters-and-creatures.md#from-definition-to-live-combatant)). A slot left inactive by the reset keeps its last creature until it is spawned again, which the clean check does not look at. Since the fix a soak seed gives the same trace hash in a batch session as alone in a fresh session (seeds 21-40 checked, section 3.5). Being `internal`, they are reachable from the harness in Assembly-CSharp but not from an MCP `CommandScript`.
- `CharacterCreationUI.CompleteWithParty(party, flowSource)`: the end of Play Now! and Quick Start, callable with any non-empty party (returns false and changes nothing for a null or empty one).
- `Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioFastMode` (editor only, public): `Apply("fast")` sets timeScale 30, captureFramerate 30, maximumDeltaTime 1, uncapped frame rate, run in background, logs below Warning filtered and dice logging off; `Apply("watch")` is real time with every other saved setting back (logs and dice logging visible again); any other mode is refused. `Restore()` puts the saved settings back. QualitySettings (vSync) are never written, so nothing can leak into ProjectSettings. `StartProbe()` and a later `ProbeResult()` measure waits under fast mode; a mode the harness had already applied stays applied afterwards.
- **Silent stalls.** Console Error Pause pauses Play on any `LogError` or exception: when polling a run, check `EditorApplication.isPaused` and unpause (or turn Error Pause off before a run). The other stall is editor throttling when Unity is not focused (see the probe below). A third, seen on 2026-10-09, is a stall on entering Play mode, focused or not (TST-036; the batch 7 result below and section 3.5), probably from domain reloads that grow slower over a long editor session (TST-037).

**Fast-mode probe of 2026-10-07** (Play mode, editor focused, MainScene at character creation): every `WaitForSeconds(0.8f)` and every `WaitForSeconds(0.08f)` took exactly 1 frame (20 of each), and each frame advanced scaled time by 1.0 s (captureFramerate 30 x timeScale 30; maximumDeltaTime 1 did not clamp it lower). The 40 waits took 41 frames and 0.073 s of real time (about 1.5-1.8 ms per frame); the game ran at about 650 frames per second between MCP calls. Every scaled wait in game code therefore costs one frame, and anything paced by `Time.deltaTime` jumps 1 s per frame (poison secondaries, CMB-007). Settings were restored afterwards (timeScale 1, captureFramerate 0, maximumDeltaTime 0.333). That probe also set vSync, which fast mode no longer touches. A second probe of 2026-10-07 (after the seams review, the probe now counts frames with and without editor focus) gave the same numbers (41 frames, every wait 1 frame, 0.07-0.14 s real time), with fast mode applied by the probe and again with fast mode already applied by the caller (it stayed applied afterwards). Unity reported the editor focused on all 42 frames (`InternalEditorUtility.isApplicationActive`). The batch 7 full regression of 2026-10-09 measured the unfocused case: every job of rules run 20261009-081350 (545 jobs), smoke run 20261009-082000 and soak run 20261009-082525 counted all its frames as unfocused (`editorFocusedFrames` 0) and, once the session had started, ran at normal speed (rules and smoke jobs at most 7-10 s, soak jobs at least 35 frames per second). Entering Play mode is another matter: the first job of the rules session and of every soak session took 84 to 108 s (10 to 667 frames, about 0.1 to 6 frames per second), whether the editor counted as unfocused (runs -081350 and -082525) or focused (soak runs -083038, -084007, -084521 and -085027), while the smoke session did not stall (first job 7.7 s, 15 frames). The `EditorApplication.QueuePlayerLoopUpdate()` call in `ScenarioBatchDriver.WaitAndStart` did not get Play mode past that stall; see TST-036 and the procedure in section 3.5. In the 2026-10-07 probe session a `Debug.LogException` did not pause Play (Error Pause was off).

### 3.4 Scenario harness

`Assets/Scripts/Tests/Scenarios/` (all `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, namespace `Tests.Scenarios`; public so an MCP `CommandScript` can call it) plays real fights: the real `StartCombat`, turn order, AI and rules code, with the actors on exact squares, seeded dice, optional forced dice and a typed trace. Built 2026-10-07 on the seams of section 3.3.

**Expected rules verdict until fixed (batch 13 midpoint regression, 2026-10-29, run 20261029-204731).** The expected `rules/*` verdict is FAIL from `combat-end-defeat-ally` seeds 2 and 3 only (TST-047, a stale scenario premise since batch 13 step 7), until that scenario is rewritten with typed steps for the orc; any other Fail is a regression. Before the midpoint the list was empty, and the batch 12 follow-up regression confirmed it (run 20261029-062354, 0 Fail on seeds 1-5). Its last jobs, `large-encounter-goblins` seed 2 and `large-encounter-sizes` seeds 2-5 (CMB-199, a game regression), left it on 2026-10-29 when CMB-199 and CMB-132 were fixed (both scenarios Pass on seeds 1-5, runs 20261029-055301 and, after the review, 20261029-061720; confirmed by the full `rules/*` sweep of the follow-up regression, run 20261029-062354). The 27 jobs of the stale scenarios (TST-043 to TST-046: `bard-fascinate-ai`, `bard-fascinate-scripted`, `quicken-once-per-round`, `maneuver-bullrush-charge-control`, `maneuver-bullrush-charge-reflexes`, `turned-undead-flees-ai` and `cast-combat-end-retaliation-ui`) left the list on 2026-10-29 when their fixtures were updated. Any Fail is a regression; a job listed here that passes means its issue is fixed, so remove it here. A job that lands on this list is not pinned by `ExpectKnown` or a waiver without the owner's go-ahead.

**Files.** `ScenarioModel.cs` (enums, `ActorSource`, `ActorSpec`, `DiceForce`, `Waiver`, `Expectation`, `ScenarioDef`, the `Scenario.Define(...)` builder and `ScenarioCatalog`), `ScenarioRunner.cs` (the job loop on its own DontDestroyOnLoad `ScenarioRunner` object, never on GameManager, CORE-013), `ScenarioTrace.cs` (events, JSON writer, hash), `ScenarioChecks.cs` (invariants, combat-end detection, watchdog), `ScenarioExpect.cs` (`TraceView`, `Expect`, verdict rules), `ScenarioSteps.cs` (typed steps, the AI-path executor and the Ui driver), `KnownIssueWaivers.cs`, `AiProfileForClass.cs`, `ScenarioHarness.cs` (the public API), `ScenarioTraceDiff.cs` (the first divergence of two runs of a job, section 3.5), `ScenarioBatchDriver.cs` (fresh-session batches, section 3.5), `SoakStats.cs` (soak statistics, section 3.5), `Catalog/*.cs` (scenario definitions: any `public static IEnumerable<ScenarioDef>` method marked `[ScenarioSource]` in a `Tests.Scenarios*` namespace is picked up). Wrap each `yield return` of a source in `ScenarioCatalog.Safe(name, () => ...)`: a definition that fails validation is then recorded in `loadErrors` and the rest of the source still loads.

**Actors and control.** An actor is `ActorSource.QuickStart(class)` (a class Quick Start character, through `Harness_SetupPartyFromCreation`), `ActorSource.Stats(() => stats)` (an exact `CharacterStats` in a party slot; set BAB through `BaseAttackBonusOverride`, CHR-068) or an NPC id (a pool slot, through `Harness_SpawnEnemies`). At most 4 party-slot actors (QuickStart first, then Stats, in definition order) and 40 NPCs (`ScenarioLimits.MaxNpcActors`; the game's enemy pool grows past its 15 starting slots, ENC-001); positions are validated against the 20x20 grid and placed exactly with `MoveToCell`. An NPC added with `.NpcPlacedByGame(key, id)` (`ActorSpec.GamePlaced`) has no position: the harness passes (-1,-1), the game's default layout places it as it places a random encounter (`EncounterSpawnPlacement`), and the runner leaves it there (the actor event's `pos` records the square); an exact actor whose square it took fails setup. A definition can also generate actors per job with `.GenerateActors(ctx => ...)`: it runs right after the RNG is seeded with the job seed (so a seed always gives the same actors), its actors join a per-job copy of the definition that is validated again, its `Info` goes to the `generated` trace event and the job result, and its `Cleanup` runs after the job's reset. `ActorSource.Npc(id, label)` shows `label` in the trace instead of an id made per job. Control per actor:

| Control | Turn path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Ai` | `AIService.ExecuteNPCTurn` | A party-slot actor is made non-controllable and gets a class profile (`AiProfileForClass`: Cleric and Druid Healer; Wizard and Sorcerer Evoker with a damage spell, else Spellcaster; Ranger with a ranged weapon Ranged; else Humanoid). It then takes the NPC path, not the PC path (see the limits below). |
| `Scripted` | `ExecuteNPCTurn` up to the compulsion gates, then the actor's typed steps for the round (`.Turn(key, round, steps...)`, round 0 = every round without its own), else its coroutine (`ScenarioDef.Scripts`), else an empty turn, or the AI for an actor listed in `.AiWhenUnscripted(keys)` (traced as controller `ai`) | Frightened, Panicked and Turned actors are handed back to the AI. The automatic stand-up from prone is skipped, so a script stands up explicitly. |
| `Idle` | as `Scripted`, with an empty turn | |
| `Ui` | the PC turn (`StartPCTurn`) | Party slots only. The actor's typed steps for the round run through the PC button and cell-click callbacks; when they run out (at once when there are none) the harness presses End Turn (`OnEndTurnButtonPressed`) and traces a `step` event. |

**Scripted steps** (`ScenarioSteps.cs`; the builder takes `.Turn(actor, round, params Step[])`, `.Idle(keys)` and `.AiWhenUnscripted(keys)`; the definition is validated, so a step its actor's path cannot run is a build error). Every step ends as a `step` trace event (`actor`, `path` ai or ui, index, label, `status`, `note`): `done`; `refused` (nothing changed: no game event, and the actor's square, action economy and conditions are the same; a refused AI-path `Maneuver` or `Cast` notes the standard and full-round action, whether another attack step can be committed, `CanPerformSpecialAttack` and Grappled, because fast mode filters the game's own reason); `skipped` (an `AnswerAoO` or `AnswerImprovedGrab` with no prompt open, or either on the AI path); `dropped` (the actor went down, combat ended, the turn passed, or an `EndTurn` step ran); `error` (an AI-path executor threw: `ScenarioHooks.SafeEnumerate` recorded it in `HookErrors`, which fails the job, and the script went on).

| Step | AI path (Scripted actor) | Ui path (Ui actor) |
|---|---|---|
| `Move(x,y)` | `MoveCharacterAlongComputedPathForAI`, then the move action is spent (or the standard converted) as AIService does at its own call sites; the executor refuses it through the shared movement legality (`MovementService.CanStartMovement`, batch 12 step 22: after a 5-ft step, with no move action, prone or grappling), and the step note is the refusal reason | Move button, then the square |
| `Withdraw(x,y)` | `ExecuteWithdrawMovementForAI`: the full-round withdraw, or a Restricted Withdraw (a standard action at speed) for a creature limited to one action; refused by the shared movement legality (blinded, after a 5-ft step, no action) with the reason as the note | Withdraw button, then the square |
| `FiveFootStep(x,y)` | `TryTakeFiveFootStepForAI` | 5-Foot Step button, then the square |
| `StandUp()` | `TryStandUpFromProneForAI` | Stand Up button (the AoO confirmation follows) |
| `Crawl(x,y)`, `DropProne()` | since batch 13 step 12: the crawl and drop-prone entries through `RunAIAction` (refused with the executor's reason) | Crawl button and square; Drop Prone button (both through `RunPlayerAction` since step 12) |
| `Reload()` | since batch 13 step 12: the reload entry through `RunAIAction` (refused with `ReloadRules.Check`'s reason) | the Reload button (`OnReloadButtonPressed`, through `RunPlayerAction`); a threatened actor's attack-of-opportunity prompt follows (answer it with `AnswerAoO`) |
| `AidAnother(ally, opponent, defense)`, `WakeAlly(ally)`; `ActionAgainst(actionId, t, opponent, variant)` | since batch 13 step 13: the aid-another entry (`Target` the ally, `Opponent` the foe, `Variant` offense or defense) and the wake-ally entry through `RunAIAction`; `ActionAgainst` is `Action` with `ActionContext.Opponent` | the Aid Another button (`OnAidAnotherButtonPressed`): "Aid Attack/Defense" when waking is offered too, then the opponent, "Aid Offense" or "Aid Defense", then the ally; `WakeAlly`: the button, "Wake Sleeping Ally" when both kinds are offered, then the sleeper (all through `RunPlayerAction` since step 13) |
| `AttackWall(x, y, strength)` | since batch 13 step 13's review: the attack-wall entry through `RunAIAction` (`Variant` weapon, or strength for the Strength check) | the Attack button, then the wall square (the attack step the button paid, `AttackWallRequest.ActionPaid`); with `strength`, the Break Wall button, then the square |
| `TurnUndead(includeTurned)`, `Rage()` | since batch 13 step 16: the turn-undead entry (with a `TurnUndeadRequest`: `includeTurned` true turns already turned undead too, the default skips them, as the AI does) and the rage entry through `RunAIAction` (refused with the executor's reason) | the Turn Undead button, then a click on the actor's own square in the targeting preview, then the skip question's option when an already turned undead is a candidate ("Skip already turned undead" or "Include already turned undead"); the Rage button (`OnRageButtonPressed`, through `RunPlayerAction`) |
| `Attack(t)`, `AttackAgain(t)` | `NPCPerformAttackForAI`: the creature's whole attack sequence, so a full attack while the full round is free and one attack after a move | one click of the Attack button and the target square (`AttackAgain` is the next click of the iterative sequence) |

A plain `Attack` step lets the AI choose the flurry itself (`AIProfile.ShouldUseFlurryOfBlows`) | the Flurry of Blows button (declares the flurry and starts the progressive attack sequence), then the target: the first flurry step; continue with `AttackAgain` or a `Maneuver` step, as in any PC attack sequence |

A plain `Attack` step lets the AI choose the smite itself (`AIProfile.ShouldDeclareSmite`) | the Smite button (it declares; refused when nothing was declared), then the Attack button and the target: the first attack of the sequence |

| `NaturalAttack(t, name)` | not allowed (Ui only) | one natural-attack button press for the natural attack `name` (the first unused one of that name, or a used one while Haste's extra natural attack is unused, as `ActionButtonPanel.BuildNaturalAttackButtonOptions` offers it; `OnNaturalAttackButtonPressed`) and the target square; the click is a step of the attack sequence with that attack (batch 13 step 17), so `AttackAgain` may follow it |

While the step is in flight the coroutine's optional 5-foot step prompts are skipped (a click on the actor's own square, as a player skips; noted once), and Haste's natural-attack chooser (`GameManager.HasteNaturalAttackMenuName`, CMB-124) is answered with the option whose label starts with `hasteAttack (`, or Cancel (the default natural attack) when `hasteAttack` is null or not offered; the answer is noted on the step |

| `DualWield(t)` | not allowed (Ui only) | the Dual Wield button (`OnDualWieldButtonPressed`), then the target: the PC's two-weapon full attack (origin D; since batch 12 step 18 the Full Attack flow with both weapons' steps through `RunAttackSequence`, `AttackSequenceRequest.ForUiTwoWeaponFullAttack`, its 5-foot step prompts skipped; added 2026-10-28, batch 12 step 15 review) |
| `Cast(spellId, t, metamagic)` | `TryNPCPerformSpellCastForAI` with `SpellDatabase.GetSpell(id).Clone()` (never the template) and the step's metamagic (since batch 11 step 21; the NPC path applies and spends it as the PC menu does); an area-routed spell (`AreaAimSearch.IsAreaCastForAI`, Prayer included) goes through `TryNPCPerformAreaSpellCastForAI` at the aim search's best aim whose area holds `t` (since the batch 11 step 25 review) | Cast button, the first unused prepared slot with that spell (for a spontaneous caster the spell from `GetCastablePreparedSpells`, the menu's list, since 2026-10-14) through `Harness_SelectSpell` (a melee touch spell's Cast Now / Discharge Later prompt is answered Cast Now through `Harness_AnswerTouchSpellPromptCastNow` and noted on the step; `Harness_PendingPrompt` reports it as `touch-spell`), then the target; a self-centered burst (Bless, Prayer) opens a preview instead, which the step confirms through `Harness_ConfirmSelfAoE` (the player's left click; added 2026-10-09) |

| `CastAt(spellId, x, y, choices...)` | not allowed (Ui only; the NPC path casts at an actor) | as `CastChoosing`, but the click goes to the square (x, y): a Summon Monster or Summon Swarm destination (the creature list of `ShowSummonCreatureSelection` answers `*` or a label prefix too, through `CombatUI.Harness_FindSummonCreatureOption`) or a Grease area's anchor (added 2026-10-15, batch 11 step 10) |
