| `Convert(sacrificedSpellId, level, t, metamagic)` | not allowed (Ui only) | A cleric's spontaneous conversion: the Cast button, then the spell list's Convert button on the prepared spell of that level and the metamagic panel's choice (`Harness_SelectSpontaneousConversion`, which calls `CombatUI.BeginSpontaneousConversion` as the button does), then the cure or inflict spell's target as `Cast` (touch prompt answered Cast Now). With metamagic the cast core gives up a convertible prepared spell of the adjusted level (added 2026-10-16, batch 11 step 21) |
| `UseItem(itemId, t)` | not allowed (Ui only) | `TryUseConsumableFromInventory` with the first pack item of that ItemDatabase id (the Use Item panel's call, which runs the use-item entry through `RunPlayerAction` since batch 13 step 14: a stored item is retrieved first, a move action that provokes, D7), so a scroll or wand spell enters the cast pipeline (`InitiateScrollCastThroughPipeline`, `InitiateWandCastThroughPipeline`); the target's square is clicked as soon as the target selection opens, after the AoO confirmations the item use raises (answer them with `AnswerAoO` steps); a selection that never opens is noted (added 2026-10-15) |
| `Action(actionId, t, variant)`, `ActionAt(actionId, x, y, variant)`, `ActionItem(actionId, itemId, t)`; `ScenarioBuilder.Action(actor, round, actionId, ...)` | the catalog entry through `GameManager.RunAIAction` (batch 13 step 6); refused with the executor's reason when it needs a caller's request (a cast, an overrun path) or cannot start | the same entry through `RunPlayerAction`, then its UI follow-up (a refusal or a cancel is the step's note; an AiOnly entry is refused, batch 13 step 18); `variant` is `ActionContext.Variant` (a wild shape form, a bardic music choice), the item is the main weapon, the right or left hand's item or a pack item with that id (an id not in `ItemDatabase` is a build error; one the actor does not carry is noted "item <id> not carried"). On the AI path a grappling actor's `Action` step with move, withdraw, 5-foot step, attack, full attack, flurry, smite, charge, bull rush charge or overrun is refused, as the typed steps are. Harness code in `namespace Tests.Scenarios` writes `global::ActorSource`. `ActionItem` runs a pack item through the use-item entry on the AI path since batch 13 step 14 (`rules/potion-drink-provokes-ai`, `rules/potion-drink-interrupted-ai`, `rules/scroll-casting-time-ai`, `rules/wand-no-aoo-ai`) |
| `AnswerAoO(Proceed/Defensive/Cancel)` | skipped | `Harness_AnswerAoO` while the confirmation is open; an answer not offered is refused and the confirmation answered Cancel (never Proceed) |
| `Pass()`, `EndTurn()`, `Assert(name, check)`, `Wait(frames)` | nothing; end the turn (later steps dropped); an `assert` event with the result (`Expect.AssertsPass`); wait | the same (End Turn button) |

On the AI path a grappling actor's movement and ordinary attack steps (typed, or `Action` with those entries) are refused: a script bypasses the grapple turn rules (`RunGrappleTurnForAI`), so leave such turns to the AI. The game also gives a grappling creature no ordinary movement (`GetCurrentMoveRangeSquares` is 0, PHB p.156), whoever controls it. The AI-path executors are yielded as nested coroutines, so `SafeEnumerate` catches their exceptions. On the Ui path a step acts only on a fresh frame when the actor is the active PC, the sub-phase is ChoosingAction and `Harness_PendingPrompt` is null. A click that chose nothing (an invalid square) is cancelled back to the action menu and the step ends refused. An AoO confirmation with no `AnswerAoO` step next is answered Proceed and noted on the step in flight, or traced as its own auto `AnswerAoO` step when none is in flight. A step settles when the action menu returns, the turn passes or combat ends; one that does not settle, or a menu that does not come back, within 600 frames AND 30 game-seconds (both, as in the core watchdog; fast mode spends about one game-second per frame, while watch mode runs hundreds of frames per real second) ends the job as SoftLock with the diagnosis. When the game ends a Ui turn inside a step and the next turn is another Ui actor's, the runner abandons the old driver first (its in-flight step is traced, the rest dropped). The Improved Grab menu (`ImprovedGrabMenu`) is answered from an `AnswerImprovedGrab` step, else Skip, the grapple damage-mode menu by the `GrappleDamage` step, and the hold damage-mode menu (`GrappleHoldDamageModeMenu`, opened by Pin, Escape, Move and Use Opponent's Weapon while Improved Grab hold damage applies) by `GrappleAction(kind, prefix)`, or `Lethal damage` for a plain `GrappleAction`. Other prompts are not answered and end a Ui job that way: the ranged retarget, the full-attack 5-ft choice and other special-style submenus (`Harness_PendingPrompt` reports these three as `ranged-retarget`, `full-attack-5ft` and `submenu`), and bull rush push and follow, the disarm item choice and the dual-wield prompt. The rules scenarios strip the Fighter kit's shield and spiked gauntlet from Ui fighters so no dual-wield prompt opens. Not exercised by any catalog scenario yet: on the Ui path `Cast`, `DropProne`, `StandUp`, `FullAttack`, and `Escape` without a square; on the AI path `StandUp` (`rules/prone-ai-stands` uses the AI, not a step); `Assert` and `Wait` on either path, and `EndTurn` on the AI path. Expectation helpers for steps: `TraceView.Steps`, `TraceView.LogInts` (integers parsed from combat log lines), `Expect.StepStatus`, `Expect.AssertsPass`, `Expect.Controller`.

**Job phases** (per scenario, seed and repetition; `Start` only schedules the run, and the first job begins on the next frame on the runner's own coroutine): preflight (Play mode, a ready GameManager, the project path; refused with `needsFresh` after static suites in the same Play session or after a dirty job), boot once per Play session (`CharacterCreationUI.CompleteWithParty` with the Quick Start party, the real creation path; default Fighter, Rogue, Cleric, Wizard), reset and clean check (`Harness_ResetWorld`, then no active pool slot, every `NPCs` entry a pool slot (`CharacterController.IsEncounterPoolSlot`; before ENC-001 the check compared the list's length with the first job's, which a grown pool would break), no extra live controller, no area effect, the GameEventSystem subscriber counts of the first job, no hook left set; a failure ends the job as Contaminated and stops the run), seed (`Random.InitState(seed)`, HP mode Average), spawn and place, control, hooks (trace, invariants, dice filter, input suppression, log listener, fast mode), start (`Random.InitState(seed * 7919 + 17)`, `Harness_StartCombat`), monitor (every frame), halt (twice, a frame apart, CORE-003), finalize, cleanup (hooks cleared, world reset, party rest, and control, profiles, RNG, HP mode and fast mode restored; each step guarded on its own). The whole party is rebuilt every job, so repetitions start from the same state. An exception that escapes any phase ends that job as Exception with a result, runs its cleanup, marks the session dirty and stops the run, so status.json always reaches a final state. Only profiles the harness created are destroyed; an `ActorSpec.Profile` override should return a fresh `ScriptableObject.CreateInstance` (an asset, or an instance another controller uses, is assigned but never destroyed).

**Running it through the Unity MCP.** Never edit scripts or call `AssetDatabase.Refresh` while a run is going. Depending on Preferences > General > Script Changes While Playing (not checked on this machine), a recompile either stops Play mode or reloads the scripts in place; either way the run is lost, and the runner writes status.json with `"state":"interrupted"` and a summary with run verdict INTERRUPTED. Exit Play mode and start a fresh session. Do not run the static suites during a run either: `StaticSuiteRunner` refuses while a run is in progress, and a pass that slips through ends the job as Contaminated.

1. `bash tools/compile_check.sh`; in edit mode `AssetDatabase.Refresh()` so Unity compiles the change.
2. `EditorApplication.EnterPlaymode();` (a fresh Play session; never one that ran static suites).
3. In a later command: `Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioHarness.Start("smoke/*", "1-3", "repeat=2")`. Filter: comma-separated id globs. Seeds: `1`, `1-5`, `1,3,7`. Options (`key=value;...`): `mode=fast|watch`, `maxRounds=N`, `repeat=N` (compares the trace hash of each repetition per seed), `sweep=N` (seeds 1..N, aggregated per id), `record=dice`, `keep` (stop after the first job and leave the world for a human), `wallCap=seconds` (default the definition's `.WallCap(seconds)`, else 120). `ScenarioHarness.Start(def, seeds, options)` runs a definition built inline in the CommandScript with `Scenario.Define(...)...Build()`, with no new file and no recompile. `ScenarioHarness.List(filter)` lists the catalog. Start returns `runId`, `jobs`, `statusPath` and `summaryPath` (absolute paths), and `loadErrors` when a catalog source threw (its remaining scenarios are missing from the run); it refuses with `needsFresh: true` in a dirty session.
4. Wait without the MCP, with a bounded loop run through Monitor or a background Bash (a foreground `sleep` is blocked in the agent environment): `for i in $(seq 1 200); do grep -qE '"state":"(done|interrupted)"' <statusPath> && break; sleep 3; done`. status.json is rewritten at most once a second while the run makes frames, at every job boundary and at the end; every write carries `heartbeatUtc` and `frame`. A heartbeat older than about 15 s while the state is still `running` means a dead run (a crash or a stopped coroutine): exit and re-enter Play mode. Or call `ScenarioHarness.Poll()` (never waits; it also unpauses the editor). `ScenarioHarness.Abort(reason)` ends the current job as Halted after its cleanup and skips the rest.
5. Read `Logs/Scenarios/<runId>/summary.json` (or `ScenarioHarness.Result()`), then grep the JSONL files.
6. `EditorApplication.ExitPlaymode();`. `ScenarioSessionGuard` clears any leftover hooks and fast mode.

**Files written** (`Logs/` is git-ignored): `Logs/Scenarios/<runId>/<id-slug>__s<seed>[__r<rep>].jsonl` (one event per line; its file name without `.jsonl` is the job id), `Logs/Scenarios/<runId>/<jobId>/caststages.jsonl` for a job that marked a cast stage (one stage per line, outside the hashed trace; section 3.5), `summary.json` (run verdict, totals, per-id aggregate, per-job results with violations, expectation lines and notes, waiver hits and `unusedWaivers`, frames, frames per second and editor-focus counts; `notRun` with a `resume` filter and seeds when the run stopped early; `loadErrors`; `warnings`, run-level warnings such as a combat-log leak the sweep had to clean up, section 3.5), `status.json` (state, `heartbeatUtc`, frame, current job and actor, totals; `summaryError` if the summary could not be written), all written through a temp file and `File.Replace` with retries, and one line per run in `Logs/Scenarios/index.jsonl` (run id, verdict, filter, seeds, options, totals, and `warnings`, the count of the summary's warnings, when there are any).

**Trace events.** Every line has `seq`, `f` (frames since the job started), `r` (round), `t` (turn index) and `ev`: `meta`; `actor` (key, team, control, source, class, level, HP, AC, touch AC, BAB, Hit Dice `hd`, racial Hit Dice `racialHd`, base saves `baseFort`, `baseRef` and `baseWill`, position, size, speed, AI profile, weapon); `init` (order with roll, modifier, total); `round`; `turn_start` (actor, controller `ai`, `scripted`, `idle` or `ui`, and a snapshot of every actor: HP, nonlethal, position, sorted conditions, HP state, grappling, team); `turn_end` (action-economy flags and the snapshots that changed); `move` (from, to, movement type, squares); `attack` (die, total, modifier = total - die, AC, hit, damage, natural 20 and 1, threat, confirmation, AoO flag and trigger, flanking and its bonus, sneak attack, ranged, weapon, weapon damage dice `dice` and their roll `baseRoll` (0 on a miss; a confirmed critical's roll includes the extra dice), the static damage modifier `dmgMod` and its terms `dmgTerms` ("label:value" joined by "; ", from `CombatResult.WeaponDamageBonus`, CMB-003), the weapon damage before riders `weaponDmg` (0 on a miss), the number of times the weapon damage was rolled `dmgRolls` (the critical multiplier on a confirmed critical, else 1; 0 on a miss; CMB-004), the sneak attack damage `sneakDmg`, `critImmune` (a threat against a creature immune to critical hits: the damage is not multiplied; CMB-064), `critEffects` (that threat was confirmed, so only the weapon's critical-hit effects apply, DMG p.222), concealment miss); `aoo` (trigger: movement, maneuver, spellcast, standup, bullrush-move, ranged, item, pickup or other); `maneuver`; `threatened_cast`; `cast` (a cast begins: caster, target, spell id and level; raised by the NPC path and, since batch 11 step 3 (2026-10-15), by the PC pipelines at their cost point, `PerformSpellCast`, `PerformAoESpellCast`, `HoldPendingMeleeTouchCharge` and `TryConsumePendingSpellCast`, for scroll and wand casts too; the target is null for an area, summon, Grease or held-charge cast, and the delivery of a held charge is not a cast); `generated` (what a definition's `GenerateActors` produced, for example the DMG encounter); `cond`; `hp`; `nl`; `dice` (with `record=dice`, or whenever a force fired); `log` (combat log text without rich-text tags); `phase` (with `by`, the three nearest GameManager methods that set CombatOver; `GameManager.BeginCombatantTurn` is skipped, so the turn-start check reports `StartPCTurn` or `SingleNPCTurnFromInitiative`, as before batch 12 step 5 moved it there); `step`; `note`; `decision`; `violation`; `watchdog`; `log-leak` (the combat-log leak sweep found a leak: root lines destroyed, when, and the panel's `holders` and `lines` when they were out of bounds, section 3.5); `end` (outcome and final snapshots); `expectation` (`known` names the issue of a known-behaviour pin; the field is set only on pins); `verdict`. The trace hash is SHA-1 over every line except `watchdog` and `log-leak` events (both depend on frame timing), without the fields `f`, `rep`, `utc`, `gitHead`, `wallSec`, `mode` (fast or watch, so the two modes can be compared) and `diag` (the timing-dependent detail of a SoftLock or Timeout decision). The `meta` event's `harness` field is 6 since the attack event gained `dmgRolls`, `sneakDmg`, `critImmune` and `critEffects` (2026-10-09, CMB-004; 5 from `dmgMod`, `dmgTerms` and `weaponDmg`, 2026-10-09, CMB-003; 4 from the actor event's `hd`, `racialHd` and the base saves, 2026-10-08, CRE-004; 3 from the attack event's `dice` and `baseRoll`, 2 from the `cast` event); compare hashes only between traces of the same harness version and code.

**Hashes and method names.** The `phase` event that enters CombatOver records `by`, the first three GameManager frames above the setter by method name (an iterator or lambda reports its owning method). So a refactor meant to keep every hash (a pure move, such as batch 13 step 6) must keep the names of the GameManager methods that end a combat, or explain the shift with `ScenarioTraceDiff.FirstDivergence`; batch 13 step 6 kept `NPCExecuteBreathWeaponForAI` as the breath core's name (an overload) for this reason.

**Legal-set shadow record** (batch 13 step 6, C8). `GameManager.RunAIAction` checks each AI pick against the actor's `ActorActionSet`; a pick outside it, or a set that could not be built, goes to `ActionSetShadow` and to a `Debug.Log("[ActionSet] ...")` line. Fast mode (the default) filters Log-level lines out, so do not count `[ActionSet]` lines in the logs: read `summary.json`'s `actionSet` (`total`, `distinct`, `jobs`, and `counts` keyed "actionId: bar: reason" with picks and jobs) and each result's `actionSet` (its counts and first 20 lines). The record is cleared when each job starts and stays outside the trace hash.

**Invariants** (a broken one is a `violation` event): `hp-bounds` (HP at most max plus temporary HP; HP state consistent with HP), `grid` (on the grid, in its square's occupancy, no shared square unless grappling, the two are still in the square a pin release left them in (the release ends the grapple and moves neither, PHB p.157, CMB-089, CMB-122; the allowance is granted only when a Pinned condition ends and neither creature grapples afterwards, so a grapple ended by an escape, which must move the escaper, gets none; it ends when either leaves that square), one of the two is helpless (PHB p.148) or one is a swarm (MM p.237 and p.316); grapple opponents at most 1 square apart, or their natural reach if larger, since a grappling creature takes no ordinary movement and the grapple's own move drags its opponents along, PHB p.156-157), `turn-structure` (turn start and end pair up, one turn per actor per round, rounds never go back, no turn for a dead actor), `no-act-when-down` (no attack or maneuver by a dead, dying, stable or unconscious actor; a disabled actor, at 0 HP or at negative HP with Diehard, may act. The threatened-cast hook fires after the AoOs the cast provoked, so a caster dropped by one of them correctly loses the spell; only a spell that still goes off with the caster down is flagged), `attack-math` (a natural 1 never hits, the flanking bonus is 0 or +2, hit agrees with total against AC unless a natural 20, concealment, a protection barrier or Deflect Arrows, which the trace recognises by its "deflected" note), `econ` (no full-round action when the turn started disabled or staggered, no 5-ft step plus other own movement, either way round (the step is read from `CharacterController.HasTakenFiveFootStep` since batch 12 step 22; before, the check read `ActionEconomy.HasMoved5Ft`, which nothing sets, so it never fired; it counts only `move` and `path-move` events, so it covers the NPC executors and not a Ui actor's own moves, which `GameManager.ExecuteMovement` traces as `path-reposition`), at most 4x speed (the same NPC-only count); moves are reported per segment, so the squares are a lower bound. The bull rush follow and overrun moves arrive as ordinary moves, so the squares moved since the actor's last attack, AoO or maneuver are taken back when a bull rush or overrun event arrives; whether a follow after a 5-ft step breaks the step is not settled RAW and is not flagged), `aoo-budget` (AoOs since the threatener's last turn at most 1, plus the DEX modifier with `Combat Reflexes`), `prone-move` (no own move of more than 1 square while prone, PHB p.143; the crawl), `team-stable` (no team change without Charmed or Commanded), `no-errors` (a LogError or LogAssert from game code is a violation; an exception from game code ends the job as Exception, halted by the runner on the next frame because halting inside a log callback is unsafe. Origin comes from the stack trace: a frame under `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Scenarios/` or in `ScenarioHooks.cs` is the harness, already reported as `hook-error`; no `Assets/Scripts/` frame at all, as for editor windows or an agent's CommandScript, is foreign; both only add a job note), `combat-end-detected`, `combat-end-early`, `phase-after-combatover`, `cast-stack` (the per-cast context stack was misused: `ScenarioHooks.CastStackViolation`, raised by `GameManager.BeginCast`/`EndCast` when a cast ends while another is on top, a Ui cast begins inside an AI cast or a Ui exit tries to end an AI cast; batch 11 step 4), and `hook-error` (a harness handler threw; always an Error).

**Combat end.** The harness uses the game's own predicate (owner definition 2026-10-07): `CombatEndRules.IsOutOfFight` (`Combat/Core/CombatEndRules.cs`), read through `ScenarioChecks.IsOutOfFight`, `SideState` (which reads `GameManager.GetCombatEndSides`, the counts `EvaluateCombatEnd` uses) and the snapshots' `out` flag (`ScenarioChecks.IsDownSnapshot`). A creature is out of the fight when it is dead, dying or unconscious, with or without regeneration or fast healing. Unconscious covers stable, knocked out by nonlethal damage, the Unconscious condition, asleep (the Asleep condition alone, as a sleep arrow applies it, counts) and petrified (considered unconscious: PHB p.311, DMG p.301). A disabled creature stays in, at 0 HP (PHB p.145) or at negative HP with Diehard (PHB p.93; healing at negative HP keeps a Diehard creature disabled, not stable, since 2026-10-08). A side is out when every active member of that team (party, pool and summons) is out and it has an active member or had one earlier in the combat (a side whose last creature was removed is out). Because the harness reads the game's own predicate, `combat-end-detected` and `combat-end-early` catch a missing check, not a wrong predicate: `Tests.Combat.CombatEndRulesTests` pins the predicate case by case from the owner definition. When the game sets CombatOver, the outcome is Victory or Defeat from the side states (if neither side is out, the game ended combat early: `combat-end-early`). When a side is out and the game has not ended combat by the end of that turn, the harness records `combat-end-detected`, sets VictoryUndetected or DefeatUndetected and halts the fight itself. Since the game checks at every turn boundary (`NextInitiativeTurn`), both are now unwaived failures; the `cause=hp<=0` / `cause=unconscious>0` split of the detail went with CORE-011 and CORE-037 (fixed 2026-10-08). Owner interpretations 2026-10-11 (CORE-038): a hostile creature charmed by or under the control of the party side counts as out of the hostile side (`CombatEndRules.IsControlledByTeam`, in `GetCombatEndSides`, so the harness sees it too); when both sides are out at once the game rolls the dying PCs' stabilization out and declares the outcome, and the harness takes Victory or Defeat from the handler that set CombatOver (the nearest `HandleCombatVictoryDetected` or `HandleCombatDefeatDetected` frame in the phase event's `by`, `ScenarioChecks.DeclaredOutcome`; a caller name such as `CheckCombatVictory` does not count) instead of calling every tie a Defeat.

**Watchdog.** SoftLock after 300 frames and 60 game-seconds without a new event (repeated identical log lines do not count); SkipChainRunaway when more than 3x the initiative count turns start in one frame (CORE-012; halted inside the turn-start handler); Stalemate when a round past MaxRounds begins; Timeout at the wall-clock cap; Paused on a second editor pause that no logged error just preceded (a human or debugger pause). A pause in the frame of a logged error, or the next one, is Console Error Pause: the runner unpauses it at once and only notes it, so waived errors stay usable whatever the Console toggle says. SoftLock and Timeout add a diagnosis to the job notes and the decision's `diag`: `Harness_DumpState`, the active Canvas objects whose names contain Prompt, Dialog, Confirm or Panel, and the last 20 trace lines. Contaminated mid-job when a static-suite pass ran or the hooks were cleared. A soft lock, a runaway, an exception, a contamination or a dirty reset marks the session dirty: later Starts answer `needsFresh` until a new Play session.

**Verdicts.** Error (SetupFailed, SoftLock, SkipChainRunaway, Exception, Paused, Timeout, Contaminated, or a hook error), Fail (an expectation without an XFail issue failed, or an unwaived violation), XPass (an expectation marked `ExpectXFail(issue, ...)` passed, so the issue may be fixed; reported loudly), XFail (only XFail expectations failed), Inconclusive (an expectation could not decide, or the job was aborted: outcome Halted), Known (only waived violations, or a known-behaviour pin that held: `ExpectKnown(issue, name, check)`, added 2026-10-15 for batch 11, states today's behaviour that the filed `issue` says is not the rule or not yet shown to be; a pin is not a ruling, and when it fails the job is Fail: the fix that changes the behaviour rewrites the pin as a plain expectation of the rule, anything else is a regression), Pass. A sweep aggregates per id, first match wins: Error, Fail or XPass if any seed had it; Pass if any seed passed; Known if any seed was Known; Inconclusive if every seed was; else XFail. Run verdict: INTERRUPTED (Play mode ended or scripts reloaded mid-run), ERROR (also when jobs were left without a result), LOADERROR (a catalog definition or source failed to load, so the run may be a subset; see `loadErrors`), FAIL, XPASS, NONDETERMINISTIC (a repetition's hash differed; the job's `firstDiffSeq` is the first differing line), ABORTED or OK. An OK run in which some id aggregated to Inconclusive (every seed undecided, so the run proved nothing for it) reads `OK (n inconclusive)`, and status.json and summary.json list those ids in `inconclusiveIds`: check it before trusting an OK, and widen the seed range for those ids. Expected Fail jobs: none since 2026-10-14 (TST-038 fixed with CMB-028, TST-039 and TST-040 with CRE-062); a full `rules/*` run is OK, with XFail only for the issues its expectations name. Any Fail is a regression.

**Waivers.** `KnownIssueWaivers.Global` is empty: the CORE-003 waiver for `phase-after-combatover` went in batch 12 step 6 (2026-10-28, once `rules/turn-start-acid-arrow-last-enemy` showed a tick kill ending the fight at the turn-start check), and the CORE-011 and CORE-037 combat-end waivers were deleted when those issues were fixed on 2026-10-08. A definition adds its own with `.Waive(issue, invariant, detailRegex)`. Every run lists the waivers that never matched in `unusedWaivers`; delete a waiver that stays unused after its issue is fixed. Add an error-log waiver only after seeing the real message, always with its issue ID.

**Writing a scenario.** Put it in `Catalog/<Area>Scenarios.cs`; prefer typed steps over coroutine scripts; name each expectation after the rule it checks (for example "Flanking gives +2 and leaves AC unchanged (PHB p.153, CMB-001)"); pin branch-critical dice by context with `.Force(sides, value, ctxSubstring, count)` (DiceService contexts such as "Trip touch attack"; context-free `DiceRoller` dice can be forced only by sides, and the raw `Random.Range` sites of TST-033 not at all); keep expectations structural, since any added or removed `Random` call shifts every later roll. Confirm NPC ids with `NPCDatabase.Get` first. Dice contexts in use (grep `DiceService.D20("` for the rest): "Trip touch attack", "Trip Strength check", "Trip defense check", "Touch attack" (the grapple touch attack), "Grapple check" (every grapple check, both sides; ties go to the higher modifier), "Grapple opposed check (attacker)" and "(defender)" (moving the grapple), "Bull rush check", "Bull rush defense", "Disarm attack roll", "Disarm defense roll", "Sunder attack roll", "Sunder defense roll", "Overrun attack roll", "Overrun defense roll", "Counter-trip check" (the defender's check when it trips back) and "Counter-trip resist check" (the original tripper's). Every saving throw d20 goes through `SaveRollRules` since batch 12 step 10 and its context ends in `SaveRollRules.SaveDiceTag` ("[save]"; the tag alone for a save with no context of its own), so `.Force(20, v, SaveRollRules.SaveDiceTag, -1)` forces every save; `SpellCaster.SavingThrowContext` ("Spell saving throw") is the save of `SpellCaster.Cast`, `GameManager.BreathWeaponSaveContext` a breath weapon's, `AIService.SpecialRangedTouchContext` a monster's ranged touch attack. **Save fallback** (batch 12 step 10): when an actor carries a `scenario:save-tweak` of 20 or more either way (`Bonuses.Set("scenario:save-tweak", BonusTarget.AllSaves, ...)`), the runner adds a last force of every `[save]` d20 to 10, so the tweak decides the save even though a natural 1 or 20 always decides it otherwise (PHB p.177); the scenario's own forces come first and win. Weapon attack rolls, initiative and the Concentration check (`ConcentrationManager`, `DiceRoller.D20`) have no context. Where a branch rests on such a roll, write the expectation for every branch (for example: a damaging AoO foils the disarm, otherwise the target is disarmed), return `ExpectResult.Inconclusive` when the branch under test did not come up, and run a seed range: a sweep aggregates to Pass when any seed passed and none failed.

**Limits of AI-run party members.** They take the NPC turn path (the turn-start effects, rage and bardic music are shared since batch 12 step 6, and the turn-start perception check since step 8), no walls, Summon Swarm or two metamagic feats on one cast (AI-071, AI-053, AI-072; two-weapon fighting and Rapid Shot by the AI stopgap's rules since batch 12 step 18, AI-055; area spells since batch 11 step 25, summons, Dimension Door and held charges since step 27, the AI's own metamagic choice since step 28; the AI flurries since 2026-10-14, CHR-003); see [systems/PC_NPC_PARITY.md](systems/PC_NPC_PARITY.md) section 2. The `controller` field of every turn says which path ran. PC executors are covered only by Ui actors. Prompts other than the AoO confirmation and the counter-trip prompt (the ranged retarget, the full-attack 5-ft choice, a special-style submenu, bull rush push and follow, Improved Grab, the disarm item choice, the dual-wield prompt; the touch-spell prompt is answered Cast Now by the Ui `Cast` step) are not answered yet and end a Ui job as a SoftLock (see Scripted steps). The counter-trip prompt (PHB p.158, CMB-079: a controllable defender after a trip against it failed at the opposed check) can open on any turn, so the runner answers it every frame, before the Ui driver (`HandleCounterTripPrompt`, through `GameManager.Harness_AnswerCounterTrip`, the same answer as the buttons): Trip Back, or Decline for an actor named in `.CounterTripAnswer(key, false)`; each answer is a `note` event ("counter-trip prompt for <key> answered TripBack|Decline"), and `Harness_PendingPrompt` reports `counter-trip` while it is open. An AI-path `Maneuver` step settles only after the answer, as the NPC coroutines wait for it.

**Rules scenarios** (`Catalog/RulesScenarios.cs`, tag `rules`; NPC data and the PHB pages are in the file header). Stats actors are Human fighters (STR 16) with BAB set through `BaseAttackBonusOverride`.

| Scenario | Checks |
|---|---|
| `rules/movement-aoo-move`, `-5ft`, `-withdraw` | an orc leaving the fighter's reach provokes exactly one movement AoO before it leaves the square; a 5-ft step and a withdraw provoke none (CMB-005, CMB-073; PHB p.137, p.143-144) |
| `rules/movement-aoo-withdraw-far`, `-ui` | a withdraw of 9 squares, (10,10) to (19,10), away from the only enemy, at (9,10): beyond one move (a fixture step checks the mover's budget: 30 ft for the hero, 40 ft for the barbarian orc) and within the double move, ends there and provokes no AoO (PHB p.143). Scripted: an NPC orc through the NPC withdraw executor; `-ui`: a PC hero through the Withdraw button and click, which before GRID-001 (2026-10-14) was cut to one move and provoked on leaving the start square |
| `rules/movement-aoo-withdraw-large`, `-ui` | a Large withdrawer based at (10,10) (its space (10,10)-(11,11)) withdraws 6 squares west to (4,10) from a visible enemy at (11,9) that threatens (10,10) and (11,10); the first step vacates (11,10), the second (10,10), and neither provokes, since the whole starting space is exempt for the whole withdraw (PHB p.143, DMG p.29; delegated RAW reading 2026-10-14, GRID-021; before the fix the second step provoked). A fixture step checks the size, the threatened squares, the enemy's AoO and that the mover sees it. Scripted: an NPC ogre through the NPC withdraw executor; `-ui`: a PC hero under Enlarge Person through the Withdraw button and click |
| `rules/movement-through-ally`, `-ui` | a move of 3 squares, (10,10) to (13,10), whose straight path crosses an ally at (11,10), with the only enemy far away: the move ends at (13,10), its segments are contiguous (each starts where the last ended, 3 squares in all; on the Ui path every step is 1 square), the ally stays and nothing provokes (PHB p.148). Scripted: an NPC orc past a goblin through the NPC move executor; `-ui`: a PC hero past a fighter through the Move button and click, whose per-step executor before 2026-10-14 checked every step as the destination, refused the ally's square and jumped two squares |

Scripted: an NPC orc through the NPC move executor; `-ui`: a PC hero through the Move button and the AoO prompt (owner ruling 2026-10-08, CMB-128; PHB p.92, p.138) |
| `rules/flanking`, `rules/flanking-control` | Quick Start rogue and fighter: opposite allies flank with +2, the AC stays the setup AC, the rogue's hits add sneak attack; allies not opposite do not flank (CMB-001; PHB p.153) |
| `rules/prone-ai-stands` | a prone AI orc stands up and the fighter's standup AoO comes before Prone is removed (PHB p.143) |

| `rules/prone-scripted-move` | a prone scripted orc that does not stand cannot move (the hook sits before the AI's automatic stand-up) |

**Cast pipeline pins** (`Catalog/CastPipelineScenarios.cs`, tags `rules` and `cast-pipeline`; batch 11 step 3, 2026-10-15, [designs/cast_core_batch11.md](designs/cast_core_batch11.md)). They pin today's cast behaviour before the cast pipelines are merged: Assert steps record what happened as trace notes `cpp key=value` (facts), and the expectations judge the facts, a plain expectation for a rule that holds today and a known-behaviour pin (`ExpectKnown`, verdict Known) for today's behaviour that a filed issue says is not the rule; a pin is not a ruling, and the later step that changes the behaviour rewrites it. Casters are Stats-built Humans (Wizard INT 16, Cleric and Druid WIS 16, the class kit); the spells go into prepared slots as clones, and a wizard that needs a 3rd-, 4th- or 5th-level slot gets one added (the wizard table stops at 2nd-level slots, SPL-041). Targets are `target_dummy` (no weapon, so it threatens nothing) unless a rule needs another creature; saves are decided with a +-30 save tweak and the damage dice forced, so every seed gives the same facts. Every pair also checks that both casts ran (both steps `done`, one `cast` event per caster), so equal end states after two refused casts cannot pass. Verdicts on 2026-10-15 after the step 3 review (seeds 1-3, run 20261015-102844): 6 Pass, 17 Known.

### 3.5 Fresh-session batches and the AI-vs-AI soak

**Fresh-session batches** (`ScenarioBatchDriver.cs`, `[InitializeOnLoad]`). From edit mode, `Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioHarness.QueueFresh(filters, seeds, options)` queues one fresh Play session per comma-separated filter (seeds and options as for `Start`, applied to each) and enters Play mode. The option `perSession=N` is the driver's own: it also splits the seeds into sessions of N seeds (it cannot be combined with `sweep`). `keep` is refused (the driver leaves Play mode as soon as a run ends), and so is a project whose Enter Play Mode Options turn off the domain reload (the sessions would not be fresh). The queue (at most 50 entries) lives in `SessionState`, so it survives the domain reload of every Play-mode entry. A second `QueueFresh` in the same CommandScript appends to the same batch; once Play mode has started it is refused, and once the batch is idle it starts a new batch and drops the old results. In each session the driver waits for a ready GameManager (60 s at most), calls `Start`, and when the run ends (an Error outcome or an Abort ends it too) records the run id, verdict and summary path, pops the entry and exits Play mode; back in edit mode it enters Play mode again for the next entry. Leaving Play mode in the middle of a run (by hand or a crash) has the runner write its summary and soak rows at once, records that entry as INTERRUPTED and drops it; if entries remain, the batch pauses until `ScenarioHarness.ResumeQueue()` (or `ClearQueue()`), otherwise the batch's soak report is merged. A script recompile during a run (Recompile And Continue Playing) kills the run in a domain reload; after the reload the driver records the entry as INTERRUPTED in the same way and exits Play mode. A recompile on leaving Play mode (Recompile After Finished Playing) drops the pending Play-mode entry; after that reload the driver enters Play mode again for a queued, unpaused batch. `ClearQueue()` empties the queue and, with no run going, merges the batch's soak report.

Progress: `ScenarioHarness.Poll()` (field `batch`: the full state while entries are queued or running, afterwards a compact one with the batch id, the result and verdict counts, `warnings` (the sum of the runs' summary warnings, when any) and the report paths) or `Logs/Scenarios/batch.json` (state `queued`, `running`, `paused` or `idle`, the queue, `currentRunId`, `currentEntry`, `currentStatusPath` and the results; each result has `warnings`, its run's summary warning count, when there are any). batch.json is written only on changes, so its `heartbeatUtc` stands still during a long session; liveness comes from `heartbeatUtc` in the file at `currentStatusPath` (the run's status.json, written about once a second while a job runs): older than about 15 s while batch.json says `running` means the session has stalled or the editor is gone. A background loop can watch batch.json without the MCP; use an absolute path, because agent shells reset the working directory: `B=F:/DNDPrototype/Logs/Scenarios/batch.json; for i in $(seq 1 200); do grep -qE '"state":"(idle|paused)"' $B && break; sleep 3; done; grep -oE '"state":"[a-z]+"' $B | head -1`. The loop stops after 10 minutes without saying so: read the state it prints and start it again while that is `queued` or `running` (one job can take up to its wall cap, 600 s for the soak). A fresh session costs about 7 s of entering and leaving Play mode. On 2026-10-09 Play mode stalled on entry, with the editor counted as focused or not (the player loop held at frame 2 to 7 for about 80 s or more), and an entry that no MCP call reached during the stall failed with "GameManager not ready 60 s" (TST-036; section 3.3). Later that day both entries of a batch failed that way although polls reached the editor, after Play-mode reloads of about 175 s (TST-037): check the reload time in `Editor.log` first (section 3.1, notes). After the editor restart, the batch 8 batches of the same evening (reloads of about 3.2 s) had no stall in any of their seven sessions. `QueueFresh` is called from edit mode and the driver enters and leaves Play mode itself, so a batch does not depend on any MCP call made in Play mode; a failed call in Play mode does not block starting one, and its progress can be read from batch.json on disk. While TST-036 is open: (1) after `QueueFresh`, call `ScenarioHarness.Poll()` through the MCP about every 20 to 30 s for as long as batch.json says `queued` or `running` (the bash loop above only reads the file and never reaches the editor; in batch 7 every entry polled like this passed, though it is not proven that the poll is what freed the stall). (2) A result whose `error` is "GameManager not ready 60 s after entering Play mode" ran no job and wrote no trace, so it is safe to retry: note the batch's run ids (a new batch drops the old results), queue the same filter and seeds again with `QueueFresh` once the batch is idle, and for a soak merge the runs of both batches with `ScenarioHarness.SoakReport("runId1,runId2,...")`, as batch 7 did. Never edit scripts while a batch runs.

Verified 2026-10-07 (Unity 6000.4.0f1 through the MCP, editor not focused): `QueueFresh("rules/pin-release*,rules/maneuver-trip", "1,2", "")` ran two fresh sessions (runs 20261007-194641: 2 Pass, 2 XFail CMB-122; 20261007-194650: 2 Pass), each about 8 s from entering Play mode to its result, both summaries written and the editor back in edit mode with no hook left set. Exiting Play mode by hand during a run gave an INTERRUPTED result, and with nothing left in the queue no pause. After the review fixes (same day): a two-entry batch (`soak/*` seeds 1-6, then `rules/maneuver-trip`) exited by hand during job 3 of run 20261007-210928 recorded INTERRUPTED with the run's summary and soak rows already written, and paused; `ClearQueue()` then merged those 2 finished jobs into `soak-20261007-210920.json`. `QueueFresh` with `keep` was refused, and the two-session check above ran again OK (runs 20261007-211002 and -211012) with the polling loop shown above. The domain-reload reconciliation was not exercised (it needs a recompile during a batch).

**Cast-stage side channel and trace diff** (batch 11 step 2, 2026-10-15; [designs/cast_core_batch11.md](designs/cast_core_batch11.md)). The cast pipelines mark every stage of a cast through `CastStageTrace.Mark` (`Spell/Casting/Core/CastStageTrace.cs`), which raises the inert `ScenarioHooks.CastStage`: begin (the pipeline's method name), legality, cost, distraction (entangled, grappled), failure (ASF, Blink), spend, concentration on cast, provocation, counterspell, Ring of Counterspells, invisibility break, Mirror Image, target Blink, globe, `SpellCaster.Cast`, the handler that claims the cast (its method name; a handler marks only once it is past every check that can still decline the cast, so a missed Ray of Enfeeblement or Touch of Idiocy writes no `handler` line; the Sound Burst stun and the Shield Other link act and then let the generic path go on, marked `<name> (continues)`; Summon Monster and Summon Swarm mark `PerformSummonMonsterCast` or `PerformSummonSwarmCast` once the provocation lets the cast through), buff and combat end (the NPC path's combat end is marked in `TryNPCPerformSpellCastForAI`, its only `EvaluateCombatEnd` site) (raise sites: [architecture/combat-and-grid.md](architecture/combat-and-grid.md#scenario-hooks-test-instrumentation)). Outside the harness the hook is null and a mark does nothing: no log, no dice, no allocation (constant strings, or a detail built only behind `ScenarioHooks.CastStage != null`). While a job runs, the trace subscribes and keeps one JSON line per stage: `i`, `afterSeq` (the seq of the last trace event before the stage), `r`, `t`, `by` (the actor key, or `name:<name>` for an actor the trace has not keyed: the handler never registers an actor), `spell`, `stage`, `detail`. They are written to `Logs/Scenarios/<runId>/<jobId>/caststages.jsonl` when the job is finalized, only for jobs that marked a stage; the file is not part of the trace or its hash, so every trace hash is the same with or without it (checked on the reference run below).

To explain a changed trace hash, compare the two runs of the job: `Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioTraceDiff.FirstDivergence(runA, runB, jobId, ignoreEvents)` (editor only, edit or Play mode, reads files only; a run id or a run directory path; `jobId` is the trace file name, e.g. `rules_spell-save-dc__s1`, `.jsonl` optional). It compares the hashed form of the two traces (no `f`, wall-clock or host fields, no `watchdog` or `log-leak` events) event by event and returns compact JSON: `identical`, the compared event counts, and for a divergence its `index`, `seqA`/`seqB`, the two events `a` and `b` (null where one trace ended), the 4 events before it in each run (`contextA`, `contextB`), and the cast stages of each run marked from the first context event to the diverging event (`castStagesA`, `castStagesB`). `ignoreEvents` drops events by their `ev` name from both traces first (for example `new[] { "cast" }` when a change adds `cast` events for Ui casters); seq numbers and the fields that cite them (`attackSeq`, `seqs`) are then left out of the comparison. Procedure: run the job's filter and seeds in a fresh session (`QueueFresh`), read both runs' `summary.json`, and for each job whose `hash` differs call `FirstDivergence` from a CommandScript (`result.Log(Tests.Scenarios.ScenarioTraceDiff.FirstDivergence("20261015-014821", "<newRun>", "rules_spell-save-dc__s1", new string[0]));`); a pure-move step expects `identical`, a rules fix expects the first divergence at the rule it changed, and the cast-stage lines say which stage of which pipeline it was. A run of batch 10 or earlier has no `caststages.jsonl`, so its `castStages` list is empty.

**Spell routing golden file.** `Tests.Magic.SpellRoutingGoldenTests` (static suite, edit or Play mode) records for every SpellDatabase spell, from data and without casting: the `EffectType` after `SpellCategoryClassifier.ReclassifyAll`, `TargetType`, `AoEShapeType`, `SpellEffectRouting.ReachesApplySpellBuff`, the branch `BeginPendingSpellTargeting` takes for a PC cast (`aoe`, `summon`, `swarm`, `wish`, `self`, `single`, or `grease` for Grease, whose branch is the caster's mode choice) and whether a single-target request refuses it on data (an area-routed spell, `AoESystem.RoutesToArea`: "area-needs-aim" for every caster since batch 11 step 25, which replaced the NPC-only refusal of AI-001; the column keeps its name `npcRefuses`; the step's review added Prayer, the one Self spell with a burst, so 63 rows are true). It compares them with `tools/tests/spell-routing-golden.json` (one spell per line, ordinal id order; 292 spells on 2026-10-15: 52 `aoe`, 153 `single`, 76 `self`, 8 `summon`, 1 each `swarm`, `wish` and `grease`; 62 refused by the NPC path); a changed, added or removed spell is one failure naming it, so the suite's `passed` in the baseline is the spell count plus two. After a deliberate routing change (a new spell, a reclassification, batch 11's area casting for NPCs), regenerate the file from an edit-mode CommandScript with `result.Log(Tests.Magic.SpellRoutingGoldenTests.WriteGolden());`, update the baseline's `passed`, and list every changed spell in the commit body. The PC branch and NPC refusal are hand copies of those two methods' decision order, not calls into them (both methods carry a comment that points here; keep them in step): the suite catches routing data changes (reclassification, target type, shape, `SpellEffectRouting`), while a change to the routing code that leaves the data alone passes it and must be checked by the rules scenarios. Some rows encode known defects and are expected to change when those are fixed: `calm_animals`, `consecrate`, `desecrate`, `wall_of_thorns`, `persistent_image`, `chaos_hammer`, `holy_smite`, `orders_wrath` and `unholy_blight` were `Area` with no shape and routed as `single` for a PC until batch 11 step 23 (2026-10-16) gave them their areas (SPL-042, SPL-046); since then the PC branch follows `AoESystem.RoutesToArea` (an Area target type or a shape, the summons first) and the file has 292 spells: 63 `aoe`, 141 `single`, 77 `self`, 8 `summon`, 1 each `swarm`, `wish` and `grease`; 63 refused by the NPC path. Twelve rows changed in step 23: `bane` (now `Area` with a burst, `aoe`, refused by the NPC path, and Control: its new mind-affecting flag makes `SpellCategoryClassifier` file it so, as Crushing Despair) and `sound_burst` (now `Area` with a burst, `aoe`, refused by the NPC path), `chaos_hammer`, `holy_smite`, `unholy_blight`, `consecrate`, `desecrate` and `calm_animals` (burst, `aoe`), `orders_wrath`, `wall_of_thorns` and `persistent_image` (cube, `aoe`) and `passwall` (`Self`, `self`, no longer refused). Verified 2026-10-15: generated with 292 spells; 294/294 in edit and Play mode; with Acid Fog's golden effect type edited to Damage the suite failed with `spell routing changed: acid_fog` (REGRESSION), and passed again once the file was restored.

**Combat-log leak sweep.** Until 2026-10-08 every combat log call left about 50 inactive `PooledLogMsg` root objects behind (UI-001): a session reached 175,466 of them after 28 soak fights and fell below 1 frame per second, and the sweep destroyed 919,509 in the 50 soak fights below. `CombatLogPanel` now builds its line pool once and keeps free lines under an inactive `CombatLogPool` child, so no `PooledLogMsg` is ever a scene root. The pool creates a line only when it has no free one, so the panel holds at most `CombatLogPanel.MaxLineObjects` = 501 line objects (500 visible plus the one taken before the oldest is trimmed); the pool's configured cap of 550 free lines is never reached. The sweep stays as a safety net: every 30 frames, before the job is finalized and after its cleanup, `ScenarioRunner.SweepLogLeak` destroys any inactive `PooledLogMsg` root and checks the game's panel (`CombatLogPanel.CountLineObjects`): more than one `CombatLogPool` holder or more than 501 line objects is a leak that is not at the root, reported but not cleaned up. Whenever it finds a leak it reports it: a console warning on the job's first find, a `log-leak` trace event per find (destroyed, when, `atF`, `atR`, and `holders` and `lines` for a panel find, recorded again only when they grew; written after the `verdict` event and left out of the hash, so the trace hash is the same with or without a leak), a job note, a run-level entry in the summary's `warnings`, the warning count in the run's `index.jsonl` line and in the batch result (`ScenarioHarness.Poll()`, batch.json). The merged soak report does not carry them. Nothing in game state or the RNG changes. Verified 2026-10-08 by creating 3 stray roots during `rules/combat-log-pool` seed 1 (one `log-leak` event, the note and warning say 3, and the hash matched the clean run) and by removing the pool guard for one run (20261008-024908: the panel find said 1,051 holders and 52,550 lines, and index.jsonl and batch.json showed `warnings` 1). After the fix, one Play session ran 30 soak fights (seeds 11-40, runs 20261008-023102 and -023121, both OK, no `warnings`): the combat log's line objects (visible plus free) went 50, 100, 192 after 10 fights, 501 after 30 (they grow with the longest log of the session, up to 501), inactive `PooledLogMsg` roots stayed at 0 and the scene's root count at 28. Per-job frame rates (editor focus not controlled) ranged from 20 to 218 frames per second and were 41 to 129 over the last 10 fights; before the fix a session fell below 1 after 28 fights. Checked through object and child counts only: the on-screen log (rendering, scrolling, `ClearLog` when combat ends) is not verified in Play mode.

**The soak** (`Catalog/SoakScenarios.cs`, `soak/dmg-random-encounters`, tag `soak`). The four Quick Start characters (3rd level: Fighter, Rogue, Cleric, Wizard, all AI-run with class profiles, on the left side) fight a random dungeon encounter from the DMG tables (DMG p.78: choose the dungeon level, roll d% on its table, which can send the roll to the next lower or higher table, and roll the number appearing; DMG p.77: a party belongs where the dungeon level matches its level). The seed picks dungeon level 1 + (seed - 1) mod 3 and, through the seeded RNG, the roll (`DungeonEncounterTableManager.GenerateRandomEncounter`, then `DungeonEncounterSpawner.PrepareEncounter` for class levels and templates; an encounter whose creatures are all missing from `NPCDatabase` is rerolled up to 5 times; the per-job `spawn_...` ids are unregistered after the job). Creatures, at most `ScenarioLimits.MaxNpcActors` (40 since ENC-001), are placed on the right half (x 11-18, y 2-17) largest first with a free square between them; the game's `CustomEncounterBuilderUI.CalculateSpawnPositions` ignores creature size, so the soak places them itself. MaxRounds 30, wall cap 600 s per job (the definition's `.WallCap`), any outcome. A job passes when the fight ends in a Victory or Defeat the game declares itself, or in a Stalemate at the round cap, no unwaived invariant broke and nothing ended as an error. The only waiver left is the global CORE-003 one; the CORE-011 and CORE-037 waivers were deleted with their fix on 2026-10-08, so an undetected end is now a Fail.

Each soak job's result carries `soak` (outcome, rounds, turns and per team: actors, down at the end, turns, attacks (every weapon attack roll, AoOs included), hits, AoOs, maneuvers and successful maneuvers, casts begun on the NPC path, own moves and squares) and `generated` (encounter name, dungeon level, target EL, creatures). summary.json aggregates them as `soak` (outcomes, verdicts, mean rounds, turns and wall seconds, per team totals, per job and per turn, and one compact row per seed), and the run writes `soak-rows.tsv`. A batch merges the rows of its runs into `Logs/Scenarios/soak-<batchId>.json`; `ScenarioHarness.SoakReport("runId1,runId2,...")` merges any runs. Any run with a `soak`-tagged scenario writes these, `smoke/soak-mini` included, so a `rules/*,smoke/*` batch also leaves a `soak-<batchId>.json`.

Run it: `ScenarioHarness.QueueFresh("soak/*", "1-50", "perSession=10")` (about 3 minutes in five sessions on a freshly started editor: batch 20261009-165858 took about 2 min 50 s, of which the jobs are 135 s and the rest is the fresh Play sessions; a much longer batch, or first jobs that take a minute or more, means slow domain reloads: check the reload time in `Editor.log`, section 3.1 notes, TST-037 and TST-036). For the determinism check, make both calls in one CommandScript so they land in one batch: `QueueFresh("soak/*", "1-3", "repeat=2")` and `QueueFresh("soak/*", "1,2", "mode=watch")`; then compare the hashes with the fast run. (Made in separate commands, the second call is refused once Play mode has started, or starts a new batch once the first is idle: note the first batch's run ids before it.)

Found by the 2026-10-08 run below: seeds 25-30 and 37-40 of this baseline are contaminated by CRE-046 (fixed 2026-10-08; recheck results after the 2026-10-08 soak below) (their enemy fought with the Babble aura and incorporeality left on the slot by the allip of seed 24 or 36), so these figures include 10 contaminated fights.

Enemy casts are 0 because no encounter in seeds 1-50 rolled a spellcaster (the creatures are in the runs' `soak-rows.tsv`). Abilities that are not spells (the dretch's spell-like abilities, the lantern archon's light rays, hell hound breath) are not counted as casts: only `GameManager.TryNPCPerformSpellCast` raises the `SpellCast` hook.

What the baseline shows (read from the traces): the AI-run cleric cast a cure spell on itself at full HP on 468 of its 624 turns (AI-047); 103 grapple attempts (86 by the party, 17 by enemies) were refused because the target was already grappling someone, and each still used the attack (CMB-121); trips dominate the maneuvers on both sides and mostly fail (party 54 of 207, enemies 42 of 227); against a locust swarm the party could not hurt it and the swarm made AoOs (AI-059, CMB-123, SPL-121); two incorporeal undead (allip, seeds 24 and 36) spawned dead (CRE-044). Stalemates with a healthy party facing one or two weak enemies (seeds 5, 7, 34, 39) come from these wasted turns; seed 39's ogre also used Babble and had 50% concealment carried over from the seed 36 allip (CRE-046, fixed 2026-10-08; with the fix and the rules of 2026-10-08 seed 39 ends VictoryUndetected in 6 rounds), so that stalemate is not a clean AI reading.

Determinism: seeds 1-3 with `repeat=2` (run 20261007-194438) gave the same hash for each repetition; seeds 1-2 in `mode=watch` (run 20261007-205259, about 20 s each at real time) gave the same hashes as the fast run 20261007-204356; seeds 1-20 gave the same hashes in one long session (run 20261007-194724, interrupted after 20 jobs) as in fresh sessions; only seed 3 of the first run (20261007-194438) differs, because the `grid` invariant then still flagged the swarm sharing a square.

The main cause, read from the traces, is the SPL-005 AI change (no cure on an unhurt creature): in batch 6 the AI-run cleric spent 348 of its 365 turns curing itself at full HP (AI-047), and now its 27 casts in 414 turns all cure a hurt creature. The turns it gained are not used. Counted on `turn_end` events (414; the traces hold 415 cleric `turn_start` events), the cleric moved on 387 turns (388 `move` events; 374 "moves to get a better shot" in 41 of the 50 seeds) and made no attack of its own (13 AoOs only). On 298 of those 387 turns (26 seeds) a party member was below the Healer's 70% threshold, so the turn was a Healing turn: the cure found no ally within touch range (the nearest such ally was 2 to 12 squares away, 3 or 4 on 205 turns), and the ranged-kiter fallback moved the cleric to 4 squares (`HealingRangeSquares`) from the enemy it picked, never toward the ally (AI-047). On 83 (38 seeds) every party member was at 75% or more, a Buffing turn, yet no buff was cast (Bless is an area spell, which the NPC cast path refuses, AI-001; Spiritual Weapon and the orisons Guidance, Light and Detect Magic were never cast either, why not was not traced), and the same move followed; 4 more were OffensiveSpell turns. The 27 casts were 12 Cure Light, 12 Cure Moderate and 3 Cure Minor Wounds. The clearest example is seed 19 (run 20261009-083038, Tiny vipers): the rogue is Disabled from round 7 and the wizard from round 13, both then Dying and Stable at -3 (from rounds 18 and 16), while the cleric, 5 squares from the rogue, steps between (11,1) and (12,1) from round 8 to the 30-round cap and cures neither. ## 4. Manual testing

### 4.1 Starting a session

Press Play in `Assets/Scenes/MainScene.unity`; `_Core/SceneBootstrap.cs` builds everything at runtime. On the character-creation screen (`UI/CharacterCreation/CharacterCreationUI.cs`):

- **Play Now!** (`OnVeryQuickStart`, line 2802) creates Fighter Aldric (Dwarf), Rogue Lyra (Elf), Cleric Theron (Human) and Wizard Elara (Elf) from each class's `GetQuickStartCharacter()`.
- **Quick Start** (`OnQuickStart`) picks a party size of 1-6 from the 11 PHB quick-start characters. Only PC1-PC4 exist and `GameManager.SetupCreatedCharacters` stops at 4, so sizes 5-6 probably drop the extra characters (not verified in Play mode).

Then the Encounter Selection UI opens (`GameManager.PromptEncounterSelection`, `_Core/GameManager.cs:785`), followed by the Pre-Combat Hub (`UI/Encounter/PreCombatHubUI.cs`: Manage Inventory (Stash), Open Store, Prepare Spells, Crafting Workshop, Start Encounter, Back to Encounter Selection).

### 4.2 Test encounter presets

24 presets in `NPCDatabase.ListEncounterPresets()` (`Character/Creatures/NPCDatabase.cs:90-117`) are test scenarios. `GameManager.ApplyEncounterPreset` (`_Core/GameManager.cs:1769`) matches the id against the constants at `GameManager.cs:100-121` and calls a `Configure<X>TestParty()` method in `_Core/GameManager.TestConfigs.cs`. Those methods re-`Init` PC1-PC4 with fixed stats and deactivate unused PCs. The replacement persists: picking a normal preset next only re-activates PCs (`RestoreStandardPartyLayout`), so restart Play mode to get your created party back (CORE-004 in [issues/CORE.md](issues/CORE.md)).

| Preset id | Active PCs | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `test_2_goblins`, `xp_levelup_test` | your party | No handler; standard layout. `xp_levelup_test` is one CR 15 "XP Pinata Goblin". |
| `grapple_test`, `feint_sneak_test`, `celestial_template_test`, `fiendish_template_test`, `ogre_battle_test`, `npc_magic_missile_test`, `disrupt_undead_test` | 1 | |
| `wizard_spell_test`, `true_strike_test`, `cleric_spell_test` | 1 | Level 20 caster (Wizard: Archmage Theron; Cleric: High Priestess Ilyra) with every implemented class spell auto-prepared, vs `target_dummy`. `true_strike_test` reuses the wizard setup. |
| `turn_undead_test`, `shield_bash_test`, `summon_monster_test` | 2 | |
| `armor_targeting_test`, `tiger_hunt_test` | 3 | |
| `grease_test` (2), `protection_from_evil_test` (1), `wind_dispersion_test` (2, displayed as "Obscuring Mist Test"), `obscuring_mist_ranged_only` (3), `charm_person_test` (2), `sleep_spell_test` (1), `mirror_image_test` (1) | as shown | **Spell preparation probably broken.** See below. |

The last row's presets set `PreparedSpellSlotIds` to level-1+ spells only (`GameManager.TestConfigs.cs:159, 1021, 1104, 1150, 1278, 1568, 1636, 1702`). `SpellcastingComponent.ApplyPreparedSpellSlotIds` (`Spell/Components/SpellcastingComponent.cs:1258`) fills slots by index, slots start with level 0, and `IsValidSpellForSlot` (:1446) requires an exact level match, so the entries are rejected and auto-prepare is skipped. Expect Console warnings `Cannot prepare level 1 spell in level 0 slot!` and `Ignored invalid prepared spell`. The fix is to pad with cantrips first, as `ConfigureNpcMagicMissileTestParty` does (:933). Until then, cast through the F12 panel or try the hub's Prepare Spells (not verified).

### 4.3 F12 Spell Testing Panel

`UI/Spells/SpellTestingPanel.cs` is added to the canvas unconditionally (`SceneBootstrap.cs:193`, no debug-build guard) and toggled with F12 (`Update`, line 92; key check at :94). It lists every `SpellDatabase` spell (placeholders shown with a darker background), filters by text and level, offers metamagic toggles, and keeps damage/save/SR counters.

`CastSpell` (line 1096) works only during a PC's turn (`gm.ActivePC` must be non-null; otherwise it logs "No active PC!"). Bypasses applied to that PC, so do not treat results as normal play:

- A non-caster temporarily gets a Wizard 10 class level and a `SpellcastingComponent` (`EnsureTemporaryCasterSetup`).
- +4 to the casting ability (`ApplyAbilityBoost`); `Update` restores it (and the temporary Wizard setup) once `GetTestPanelCaster()` returns null.
- `EnsureSpellAvailable` adds the spell to known and prepared lists regardless of class list or caster level, adds a slot at the spell's level if none is ready, sets `SlotsRemaining` to 99 and un-uses spent slots holding that spell.
- `GameManager.TestCastSpellFromPanel` (`_Core/GameManager.TestPanel.cs:43`) forces `CurrentPhase = PCTurn`, opens the cast's own context (`BeginCast` with a clone of the template, the metamagic applied, and a `TestPanel` `CastSource` whose `TestPanelBypass` flags are `Components` and `ArcaneFailure`, plus `Slots` for infinite slots; batch 11 step 4), and calls `BeginPendingSpellTargeting`. `OnCellClicked` falls back to `GetTestPanelCaster()` (`GameManager.CombatActions.cs:558`). Because `ActivePC` already requires `PCTurn` (`GameManager.cs:282-291`), forcing the phase has no effect in practice, and the class comment's claim that the panel works outside a PC turn is outdated (UI-021, UI-046 in [issues/UI.md](issues/UI.md)).
- For the whole cast, three checks are skipped: the arcane spell failure roll (`GameManager.TryRollArcaneSpellFailure`, the `ArcaneFailure` flag), the component test of the cast core's Legality stage and the spend of priced material components (the `Components` flag; `SpellComponentRules.IsExempt`, one rule for every caster since batch 11 step 17: the pouch, the divine focus, priced foci and material components, Stoneskin's diamond dust included). Since batch 11 step 4 (2026-10-15) the flags are the cast's own: they hold through a single-target, touch or self cast's resolution as well as an area, summon, Grease or held-touch cast (every path makes the component test since batch 11 step 15, and every caster since step 17), and they end with the cast, which also forgets the panel's caster, so nothing leaks into the next cast or an NPC's (SPL-036, fixed; checked by `rules/stale-cast-state-f12-bypass`). `infiniteSlots` sets the `Slots` flag, which nothing reads (UI-046).

### 4.4 Other dev hooks

Left Ctrl+H cycles the HP calculation mode (`Utilities/DebugCommands.cs`). `Identifiers/EnumTest.cs` and `IdentifierTest.cs` are editor-only `[ContextMenu]` smoke checks, not attached anywhere. There are no other test scripts: the root Python scripts `phase5_validation.py` and `test_range_calculator.py`, which tested Python re-implementations rather than the C# code, were deleted (read them from git history if needed).

## 5. Manual scenarios

### 5.1 Aid Another

Code: `Combat/Maneuvers/SupportActions.cs` (a `partial class GameManager`; the file's `SupportActions` class itself is empty). No preset exists; use a multi-PC party (Play Now! + `test_2_goblins`) and move characters into the layouts below (read "Orc" as any enemy). Distances are Chebyshev squares, reach-aware via `CharacterController.ThreatensWith`. Equipping a longspear for case 2 was not checked; the Store or stash may have one.

Flow:

0. Open **Special Attack** and choose **Aid Another**. The main-panel Aid Another button is always hidden (`UI/Combat/ActionButtonPanel.cs:706-707`). The entry (`UI/Combat/CombatUI.cs:1171-1174`) reads `Aid Another (Standard)` or `Aid Another (<reason>)` with reason `Used`, `Pinned`, `No ally` or `No target`, and is disabled unless `CanUseAidAnother` passes. `OnAidAnotherButtonPressed` has a pinned-to-grapple-menu redirect, but it is not reached from this menu because `CanUseAidAnother` already rejects pinned characters.
1. If both an aid target and an adjacent sleeping ally exist, a picker offers **Aid Attack/Defense** or **Wake Sleeping Ally**; otherwise this step is skipped.
2. Select an enemy the initiator threatens with its equipped weapon.
3. Choose **Aid Defense (+2 AC)** or **Aid Offense (+2 Attack)**.
4. Select an ally who threatens that enemy with the ally's own weapon. Reach-weapon allies adjacent to the enemy do not qualify; unarmed or ranged-weapon allies count as threatening adjacent squares.
5. The standard action is paid first (D6), then the log shows `Attack roll vs AC 10:` with roll, modifier (the aider's melee attack modifier: `CharacterController.BuildAttackBonus` with its melee weapon or unarmed, plus the weapon's enhancement or masterwork bonus; since batch 13 step 13's review) and total; on a miss, `Aid Another failed (needed 10).` The standard action is spent either way. A grappling or pinned aider cannot aid (PHB p.156).

| Case | Layout | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Adjacent | Fighter (6,5) longsword, Rogue (6,6), Orc (7,6) | Orc listed; choose Defense; Rogue listed. With Fighter at (5,5) instead, the menu shows `Aid Another (No target)`. |
| 2 Reach | Fighter (5,5) longspear, Rogue (7,6), Orc (7,5) | Orc listed (distance 2); choose Offense; Rogue listed. |
| 3 No ally in range | Fighter (5,5), Rogue (10,10), Orc (6,5) | After choosing the aid type: `No allies in melee range of Orc!`; back to the action menu, no action spent. |
| 4 Several enemies | Fighter (5,5), Orc1 (6,5), Orc2 (5,6), Goblin (10,10), Rogue (7,5) | Orc1 and Orc2 listed, not Goblin. Select Orc1: Rogue listed. |
| 5 Several allies | Fighter (5,5), Rogue (7,5), Wizard (6,6), Cleric (10,10), Orc (6,5) | Rogue and Wizard listed, not Cleric. |

Bonus checks: each successful aider adds a +2 entry and entries stack; the first matching attack consumes them (offense: beneficiary attacks that enemy; defense: that enemy attacks the beneficiary). Unused entries expire at the start of the aider's next turn (PHB p.154; since batch 13 step 13's review, before at the beneficiary's second turn start). The Character Sheet shows an "AID ANOTHER BONUSES" section only while bonuses are active (`CharacterSheetUI.AppendAidAnotherSection`). The AI never uses Aid Another: `AIBehaviorData.UseAidAnother` exists but nothing reads it.

### 5.2 Sleep

Code: `GameManager.ResolveSleepSpell` (`Spell/Resolution/GameManager.SpellCasting.cs:5131`). Automated coverage: `Tests.Combat.SleepSpellRulesTests.RunAll()` (definition, Asleep condition, wake helper, Aid Another availability; not the HD pool).

Setup: `sleep_spell_test` makes PC1 Archmage Theron (Wizard 20, only active PC) against skeleton_archer (1 HD undead, immune), goblin_warchief (2 HD), orc_berserker (3 HD) and human_cleric (5 HD, over the cap). Its prepared list fails (section 4.2), so cast Sleep from the F12 panel on Theron's turn. Immune and over-cap creatures are dropped silently; the `Candidates: N` count excludes them.

1. **HD pool.** Cast so the 10-ft burst covers all four enemies. Log: `HD Pool: N (4d4) | Duration: R rounds | Will DC D` and `Result: K target(s) asleep. Remaining HD pool: P.` Repeat via F12 (slots refresh); N stays within 4-16.
2. **Ordering and cap.** Lowest HD first; ties broken by distance from the caster, not the burst center. A target larger than the remaining pool logs `(X HD) exceeds remaining pool (P) — skipped.` HD are deducted before SR and the Will save, so a resisting target still uses pool. human_cleric is never affected.
3. **Wake on damage.** Damage a sleeper (lethal or nonlethal): `<name> wakes from taking damage.`; Asleep is removed.
4. **Wake Sleeping Ally.** Not possible in `sleep_spell_test` (single PC). Use Play Now! + `test_2_goblins`: Elara casts Sleep (F12) on a burst that includes Aldric or the cleric Theron (Sleep affects allies; elves, including Elara and Lyra, are immune; the ally needs 4 HD or less and gets a Will save, so retry if it resists). An adjacent PC uses Special Attack, Aid Another, then Wake Sleeping Ally. Expect a standard action spent, `<aider> shakes <ally> awake.`, and Asleep plus Unconscious removed.
5. **Duration.** 1 min/level = 10 rounds per caster level (200 rounds for Theron). Use a low-level caster and end turns until `⏱ <name> wakes as sleep duration expires.`
